articles.title: Greenock: The town whose council wants migrants to move in
articles.summary: Greenock wants to attract immigrants to settle in the town and reverse its declining population.
articles.body:
A new shop opened along Greenock's fading High Street in May. Anik African Store has brought a small corner of Nigeria to the Scottish town, selling yams, plantain, okra and catfish.

It is not the only African food shop here - there is another just metres away, responding to the area's changing population.

Five years ago, locals say, it would have been rare to see a black person in Greenock. Now hundreds of Africans and refugees have moved to the area.

The local council has in fact come up with a plan to attract even more to this corner of the west of Scotland as a means of stemming its falling population.

Scottish people "are lovely and accommodating", says Anik's owner, Christianah Omilana, who came to the UK in 2021. "Immigrants will come when there is work", she adds.

The lack of work however has been a key driver of depopulation in Greenock and the wider Inverclyde area. No local authority in Scotland has been hit harder by population decline.

The number of residents in Inverclyde is 22,000 fewer than in 1981. And its current population, 78,000, is projected to fall by a further 16% over the next two decades.

Tackling the lack of people is the council's number one priority, by keeping more residents here and attracting others into the area.

It is a "lovely, friendly" town, says one of Anik's customers, Sunday, who has just moved here from Devon. He has begun a job at a hospital in Glasgow, and has come to Greenock to join his wife who works at the local hospital, Inverclyde Royal.

"If the local council can provide [jobs], everything in Greenock will change, because people [from Africa] would like to come," says Sunday.

Michael Buchanan and Adam Eley visited Greenock for the latest in a series of reports reflecting the range of challenges facing communities across the UK.

Most of Greenock's African population are working or studying in Glasgow or Paisley and have been attracted to the town by cheap housing. Many have arrived on skilled work visas, known as sponsorship, helping to bolster the health and care workforce.

Inverclyde Council's repopulation strategy is based on trying to encourage them to set down roots here, as well as attracting other legal migrants and people who've been granted refugee status to move in.

However, the lack of jobs lies at the root of the town's problems.

"It's a ghost town," says Tiffany, a mother of one, who we met at a local parent and toddler group. "There's just nothing in it. There's nothing to do, there are no shops. There is no employment."

The 29-year-old moved away from Greenock to work but came back to bring up her child. Now, she says she is facing up to leaving once more.

"I'm struggling to find jobs that suit both childcare and myself. I've considered moving from here to Paisley because there is so much more to do there."

Rummage through Greenock's industrial history and you will find a distinct heritage - in the 19th Century its status as a global hub for refining sugar earned it the nickname "Sugaropolis". Thousands of ships were also built in the coastal town over a near 300-year period.

More recently, the computer manufacturer IBM employed more than 5,000 people at its campus near Greenock. But the site closed completely in 2016.

Indeed, in the past four years, a further 1,500 jobs have vanished. Amazon, EE and a string of other companies have gone elsewhere. Just this week , the local shipyard announced it was cutting about a quarter of its workforce. Meanwhile, supporters of Greenock Morton, the local football team, have set up a fighting fund to try to stave off financial collapse at the club.

The town has been left bereft - little wonder Scotland's First Minister John Swinney is due to visit this month, to hear the problems first-hand.

While health and social care roles employ many of the Africans, job opportunities for those born locally, and refugees, can be hard to find.

"When the work disappears, people disappear," says Muriel, one of dozens of elderly residents gathered at Lyle Gateway Community Cafe, a stone's throw from the High Street.

Between games of table tennis and cheap, hearty lunches, the group remembers a vibrant town, full of people and shops they wanted to go to.

There is a despondency now, with words like "depressing" and "empty" peppering the conversation. The pensioners are sceptical too of the council's repopulation strategy. While happy for migrants to move in, they wonder how sustainable any influx would be.

The council requires hundreds more immigrants each year just to keep the population stable.

"Where would they work?" asks Pamela. "The people in Greenock can't get work [never mind] bringing in other people."

The cafe is housed in Lyle Kirk, where Jonathan Fleming has been the Church of Scotland minister for the past five years. He feels the town's depopulation crisis at first-hand. His church does "a lot more funerals than we do weddings and baptisms," he explains. "And that shift, it's a lot more dramatic than it used to be."

The church has been supporting some Iranian refugees recently and their experience is a sobering one, says Fleming. They are desperate for paid work but can't find any.

"They're wanting to contribute to the community. They want to be independent of receiving financial aid and they're not able to do it - they're actually trapped in it, in some respects."

The number of people arriving in Inverclyde from overseas has trebled in recent times, to about 750 per year since 2023. Hundreds of African migrants have now settled in the area, as well as refugees from Ukraine, Afghanistan and several other countries, many with a positive tale to tell.

As part of its repopulation plan, the council is offering English classes for those who need them and help to access skilled employment. Schools are also supported to provide an inclusive "anti-racist education".

Mo Almalarashid arrived in Greenock in 2018 as a Syrian refugee without a word of English. He says he found a supportive community and, after studying hard, he now works as a local gym instructor. "There was always people there for me," he says.

There have been tensions. A local teenager was sentenced to 10 years in prison last year for planning mass murder at the local mosque. And in June, a protest outside a local hotel housing asylum seekers resulted in one woman being charged with a hate crime , and three police officers being injured.

Yet in May's Scottish Parliamentary elections, Reform UK - which campaigns strongly for lowering immigration nationally - came a distant third in Inverclyde, about 8,500 votes behind the winning SNP candidate, and despite fielding its Scottish leader in the constituency.

Other council areas will face Inverclyde's depopulation challenge in the coming years. The populations of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are all expected to begin declining within the next decade.

Stephen McCabe, who has led Inverclyde's minority Labour-led council almost exclusively since 2007, believes its repopulation plan is beginning to take effect. The population has stabilised in the past two years, he says, largely because of immigration.

Repopulation is at the heart of everything Inverclyde Council hopes to achieve, McCabe says, from housing projects and the revamping of school buildings to, perhaps most importantly, job creation.

Michael and Adam report from communities across the UK

'Just push us into the sea': The frustration of an area failed by politics Published 18 February

'Just push us into the sea': The frustration of an area failed by politics

Why one small town with very little immigration turned to Reform UK Published 28 October 2025

Why one small town with very little immigration turned to Reform UK

What an empty car park tells us about the UK's debt problem Published 4 May

What an empty car park tells us about the UK's debt problem

Standing on the banks of the Clyde, he sees opportunities in the maritime, renewables and defence sectors, reimagining use of the river for the 21st Century - although for that, they will need significant Scottish and UK government support.

When asked about asylum seekers, who for the most part are not permitted to work as they await Home Office decisions, McCabe acknowledges there is "an unease, no doubt about it".

While the council has "willingly" participated in a Home Office dispersal scheme - accepting more than 200 people seeking asylum - he believes the area "has been allocated a disproportionate share", with a Home Office contractor said to have bought up a number of houses in the area.

But migrants and refugees who can work are welcome in Inverclyde, McCabe says.

"Without those people, our health service would really be struggling... The refugees who have come have brought benefits to this area. They will bring ambition. They'll bring children to this area."

Greenock's population is not just shrinking, it is also ageing. The lack of children means that one nursery is closing, while older people have greater health needs.

Add in the area's high levels of deprivation, and there is increasing pressure on public services amid a shrinking tax base. Those who remain, pay more - council tax rose by almost 8% locally this year.

Yet you do not need to look far for a different vision for Greenock. Just 15 minutes down the road is the centre of Gourock, once similarly deprived, which has a small, thriving High Street with independent retailers, boosted by a recent Â£5m council investment and residents with more spending power.

Local resident Matthew Quinn, a 19-year-old former member of the Scottish Youth Parliament, says Gourock has embraced its future as a commuter town and believes other parts of Inverclyde should follow suit.

The council's focus on creating lots of jobs locally is misplaced, Matthew believes. Many people now work from home, he says, and the area's proximity to Glasgow - about 40 minutes away - should be exploited.

"If we accepted that the jobs are in Glasgow, then our focus should be on public services and ensuring we have a nice environment for people to live. Then I think we would be much more successful," he says.

"It's not that [people] are desperate to leave, it's that there's no reason to stay."

That is a challenge that some Greenock residents are attempting to tackle, head on.

Derek Mitchell, infused with infectious positivity, is looking to convert a former sugar refinery next to an Aldi car park into a thriving hub that will teach and enthuse young people.

A focus on science, technology, engineering, arts and maths, he says, will provide them with skills for the future.

"If you build a sense of belonging, naturally and organically, people don't want to leave."

He has purchased the building as part of a group of locals, who estimate it will need Â£5m of investment as they continue to look for partnerships.

"A lot of people are starting to do things for themselves," he says. "They see there's potential - they're fed up of waiting."

At a time when much of the UK has concerns about immigration, Inverclyde's decision to embrace migrants and refugees makes it stand out. Its lack of people is acute, its solution, striking. Other communities will soon face a similar depopulation challenge and may look to what Greenock is trying as a possible way ahead.

Yet in May's Scottish Parliamentary elections, Reform UK - which campaigns strongly for lowering immigration nationally - came a distant third in Inverclyde, about 8,500 votes behind the winning SNP candidate, and despite fielding its Scottish leader in the constituency.

Other council areas will face Inverclyde's depopulation challenge in the coming years. The populations of Scotland, Wales and Northern Ireland are all expected to begin declining within the next decade.

Stephen McCabe, who has led Inverclyde's minority Labour-led council almost exclusively since 2007, believes its repopulation plan is beginning to take effect. The population has stabilised in the past two years, he says, largely because of immigration.
Repopulation is at the heart of everything Inverclyde Council hopes to achieve, McCabe says, from housing projects and the revamping of school buildings to, perhaps most importantly, job creation.

'Just push us into the sea': The frustration of an area failed by politics Published 18 February
'Just push us into the sea': The frustration of an area failed by politics
Why one small town with very little immigration turned to Reform UK Published 28 October 2025
Why one small town with very little immigration turned to Reform UK
What an empty car park tells us about the UK's debt problem Published 4 May
What an empty car park tells us about the UK's debt problem

Standing on the banks of the Clyde, he sees opportunities in the maritime, renewables and defence sectors, reimagining use of the river for the 21st Century - although for that, they will need significant Scottish and UK government support.
When asked about asylum seekers, who for the most part are not permitted to work as they await Home Office decisions, McCabe acknowledges there is "an unease, no doubt about it".

While the council has "willingly" participated in a Home Office dispersal scheme - accepting more than 200 people seeking asylum - he believes the area "has been allocated a disproportionate share", with a Home Office contractor said to have bought up a number of houses in the area.
But migrants and refugees who can work are welcome in Inverclyde, McCabe says.
"Without those people, our health service would really be struggling... The refugees who have come have brought benefits to this area. They will bring ambition. They'll bring children to this area."
Greenock's population is not just shrinking, it is also ageing. The lack of children means that one nursery is closing, while older people have greater health needs.

Add in the area's high levels of deprivation, and there is increasing pressure on public services amid a shrinking tax base. Those who remain, pay more - council tax rose by almost 8% locally this year.

Yet you do not need to look far for a different vision for Greenock. Just 15 minutes down the road is the centre of Gourock, once similarly deprived, which has a small, thriving High Street with independent retailers, boosted by a recent Â£5m council investment and residents with more spending power.

Local resident Matthew Quinn, a 19-year-old former member of the Scottish Youth Parliament, says Gourock has embraced its future as a commuter town and believes other parts of Inverclyde should follow suit.

The council's focus on creating lots of jobs locally is misplaced, Matthew believes. Many people now work from home, he says, and the area's proximity to Glasgow - about 40 minutes away - should be exploited.

"If we accepted that the jobs are in Glasgow, then our focus should be on public services and ensuring we have a nice environment for people to live. Then I think we would be much more successful," he says.
"It's not that [people] are desperate to leave, it's that there's no reason to stay."
That is a challenge that some Greenock residents are attempting to tackle, head on.
Derek Mitchell, infused with infectious positivity, is looking to convert a former sugar refinery next to an Aldi car park into a thriving hub that will teach and enthuse young people.
A focus on science, technology, engineering, arts and maths, he says, will provide them with skills for the future.
"If you build a sense of belonging, naturally and organically, people don't want to leave."
He has purchased the building as part of a group of locals, who estimate it will need Â£5m of investment as they continue to look for partnerships.
"A lot of people are starting to do things for themselves," he says. "They see there's potential - they're fed up of waiting."

At a time when much of the UK has concerns about immigration, Inverclyde's decision to embrace migrants and refugees makes it stand out. Its lack of people is acute, its solution, striking. Other communities will soon face a similar depopulation challenge and may look to what Greenock is trying as a possible way ahead.

articles.title: El Niño: Panama Canal to cut number of ships passing through
articles.summary: The crucial waterway's operator says low rainfall caused by the ocean pattern had led to the decision.
articles.body:
Panama Canal's operator is to cut the number of vessels passing through the key waterway due to low rainfall caused by El Niño.

The Panama Canal Authority (ACP) told shipping firms on Thursday that 32 vessels a day will be able to pass through it from 15 September, compared to 36 currently.

El Niño, a pattern of periodical sea surface warming, affects weather systems globally. This year is expected to be particularly strong, with its effects made more intense by climate change.

The shipping industry is already dealing with severe disruptions due to the Iran war causing a large reduction in the number of vessels passing through the crucial Strait of Hormuz.

The ACP said the measures were being put in place to preserve service reliability and safeguard water resources for human consumption.

It added that despite the arrival of the rainy season in Central America and some water-saving measures already being put in place in the canal, additional action was needed "to support the long-term sustainability of transit operations".

The new measures will be phased in from 3 September.

The Panama Canal greatly reduces the time and distance ships have to travel between the Atlantic and Pacific oceans.

About 14,000 ships per year use the artificial waterway - which operates 24 hours a day, 365 days a year.

As well as being a crucial route for global trade, it is also a key source of income for Panama, bringing in about $3bn (£2.2bn) a year.

In 2023, the ACP cut the number of vessels using the waterway during the last El Niño period after Panama was hit with its driest October since records began in 1950.

Since then, the authority has introduced measures to cut the amount of water it uses.

Many forecasts suggest that this year's El Niño, which is a naturally occurring pattern, could be one of the strongest ever recorded, with disruptions to weather, food supplies and economies.

El Niño set to be 'strongest in living memory', says Met Office

articles.title: Meghan enfrenta retorno ao Reino Unido marcado por tensões do passado | G1
articles.standfirst: Enquanto esteve no país, mulher do príncipe Harry foi submetida a um intenso escrutínio da imprensa e nunca chegou a se sentir integrada à família real. Pesquisa de opinião mostra que duquesa de Sussex tem imagem impopular entre britânicos.
articles.summary: Enquanto esteve no país, mulher do príncipe Harry foi submetida a um intenso escrutínio da imprensa e nunca chegou a se sentir integrada à família real.
articles.body:
A duquesa de Sussex, Meghan Markle, em evento na Abadia de Westminster, no Reino Unido, em novembro de 2019 — Foto: Matt Dunham/AP/Arquivo

Com o anúncio da volta do príncipe Harry ao Reino Unido , Meghan Markle, sua mulher, deve esperar um difícil retorno ao país, onde a duquesa de Sussex foi submetida a um intenso escrutínio da imprensa e nunca chegou a se sentir integrada à família real.

✅ Siga o canal de notícias internacionais do g1 no WhatsApp

Em entrevistas reveladoras e documentários, a ex-atriz americana de 45 anos nunca escondeu as dificuldades que enfrentou para se adaptar ao novo status após seu casamento de conto de fadas com o príncipe Harry , em 2018.

"Acho que há mais dúvidas sobre como ela vai se readaptar à vida no Reino Unido do que sobre Harry", resume Ed Owens, especialista em realeza.

Muito ligado às suas organizações beneficentes e desejoso de aproximar os filhos de sua família paterna, Harry enfrenta um desafio menor ao retornar ao seu país, enquanto para Meghan a equação é mais complexa.

Segundo informações da imprensa britânica, Meghan negocia para atuar em "Magnatas do Crime", uma série da Netflix criada por Guy Ritchie e gravada no Reino Unido .

A série, cuja segunda temporada estreia no início de setembro, conta a história de um duque que se torna um barão da droga.

Por outro lado, especialistas consideram que Meghan deve se dedicar principalmente à família — e especialmente aos filhos Archie, de 7 anos, e Lilibet, de 5, que estudarão no Reino Unido — e apoiar Harry em seu trabalho como patrono de organizações beneficentes.

Nos Estados Unidos, suas perspectivas pareciam ter se esgotado após o fim de seu contrato com a Netflix para o programa "With Love, Meghan", embora no fim de 2025 ela tenha feito uma breve aparição em um filme que ainda não estreou.

No Reino Unido , ela continua muito impopular. Segundo o último levantamento da YouGov, instituto britânico de pesquisas de opinião, publicado em julho, 61% dos britânicos não gostam dela.

E os tabloides, contra os quais o casal apresentou vários processos, podem não facilitar seu retorno.

Após a rumorosa mudança para os Estados Unidos em 2020, Harry e Meghan denunciaram os métodos dessa poderosa imprensa, que examina cada gesto da família real e persegue seus integrantes e pessoas próximas.

"Não importava o quanto eu tentasse. Se eu me comportasse bem, fizesse o que fizesse, eles sempre encontravam uma maneira de me destruir", contou Meghan em 2022, em seu documentário para a Netflix.

Meghan Markle e o príncipe Harry — Foto: Dylan Martinez/Reuters

A imprensa, no entanto, havia inicialmente recebido bem sua entrada na família real, considerando-a uma lufada de ar fresco em uma instituição com tradições centenárias.

Mas ela rapidamente despertou a hostilidade dos tabloides, que a acusaram de ser caprichosa e de rejeitar as obrigações associadas aos privilégios de sua nova posição.

Desde sua saída, Meghan se distanciou do Reino Unido e só retornou em poucas ocasiões, como em junho de 2022, para o Jubileu da rainha Elizabeth II, e posteriormente para seu funeral, em setembro daquele mesmo ano.

Em julho deste ano, Meghan e o príncipe Harry , acompanhados dos dois filhos, visitaram na Inglaterra o rei Charles III e sua esposa, Camilla, em um gesto interpretado como sinal de uma tentativa de reconciliação.

Mas seu retorno pode trazer novamente ao primeiro plano "os conflitos e questões que originalmente provocaram sua saída", como as acusações de racismo ou as preocupações relacionadas à sua segurança, afirmou Nathalie Weidhase, professora da Universidade de Surrey especializada em cultura das celebridades e monarquia britânica.

A isso se somam as tensões familiares agravadas pela publicação, em 2023, da autobiografia de Harry, "O Que Sobra".

Nela, Harry acusou, entre outras coisas, William e sua esposa, Kate, de terem preconceitos contra Meghan, o que dificultou sua integração à família real .

A entrevista concedida à apresentadora americana Oprah Winfrey em 2021 também causou comoção no Reino Unido . Nela, Meghan acusou um integrante da família real de racismo.

O especialista Ed Owens, no entanto, não espera uma nova guerra aberta.

Harry e Meghan buscam "estabilidade para sua família" e "não estão voltando para criar problemas para a realeza", considera.

articles.title: Zolani Tete, ex-campeão mundial de boxe, é morto a tiros na África do Sul | G1
articles.standfirst: Sul-africano de 38 anos foi baleado por dois homens ao chegar em casa em Mdantsane. Polícia ainda não sabe motivação do crime.
articles.summary: Sul-africano de 38 anos foi baleado por dois homens ao chegar em casa em Mdantsane. Polícia ainda não sabe motivação do crime.
articles.body:
Pugilista sul-africano Zolani Tete morre aos 38 anos — Foto: Reprodução/Instagram

O pugilista Zolani Tete, bicampeão mundial de boxe, foi morto a tiros fora de sua casa na África do Sul nesta sexta-feira (21). As autoridades ainda não identificaram a motivação do crime.

Segundo a polícia, dois homens encapuzados desceram de um carro e atiraram contra o lutador quando ele chegava em casa. Ele morreu no local. Uma mulher de 27 anos que estava com ele também foi baleada e levada ao hospital.

Ele treinava para voltar aos ringues, segundo o ministro de Esportes, Artes e Cultura da África do Sul, Gayton McKenzie, que lamentou a perda de "um dos melhores lutadores que o país já produziu".

O caso reacende o debate sobre a violência crônica na África do Sul, um dos países com as maiores taxas de homicídio do mundo.

Mesmo com queda recente nos índices, dados oficiais apontam uma média de 58 assassinatos por dia no país nos quatro primeiros meses de 2026.

Tete somou 34 lutas na carreira e foi dono de dois cinturões mundiais: o da IBF na categoria supermosca, em 2014, e o do peso-galo, em 2017.

Ele é mais lembrado internacionalmente por nocautear em 11 segundos o compatriota sul-africano Siboniso Gonya em Belfast, em novembro de 2017. Foi a paralisação mais rápida em uma luta pelo título mundial.

articles.title: Irã diz que recebeu mensagem de países vizinhos após ameaças de Trump | G1
articles.standfirst: De acordo com presidente do Parlamento, eles buscam "novos acordos de segurança e cooperação econômica". Neste sábado (22), a mídia estatal iraniana noticiou que o país concedeu permissão para que vários petroleiros iraquianos atravessem o Estreito de Ormuz.
articles.summary: Neste sábado (22), a mídia estatal iraniana noticiou que o país concedeu permissão para que vários petroleiros iraquianos atravessem o Estreito de Ormuz.
articles.body:
O presidente do Parlamento do Irã e principal negociador do país, Mohammad Ghalibaf, afirmou neste sábado (22) que o governo iraniano recebeu uma mensagem de seus países vizinhos sobre a criação de "novos acordos de segurança e cooperação econômica".

✅ Siga o canal de notícias internacionais do g1 no WhatsApp

Famílias iranianas lutam para comprar o básico enquanto EUA intensificam guerra econômica

Em um post na rede social X, Ghalibaf afirmou que as recentes declarações do presidente dos Estados Unidos , Donald Trump , que ameaçou punir os países que sigam negociando com o Irã, foi a motivação do contato.

"Recebemos inúmeras mensagens de países vizinhos sobre a formação de novos arranjos de segurança e cooperação econômica na região. Os Estados Unidos colocaram a segurança de cada um de seus aliados em um risco tão grande por meio de intimidação e total desrespeito aos seus interesses em prol de Israel, que eles brevemente viram toda a sua existência em risco", escreveu.

Mohammad Baqer Qalibaf, presidente do Parlamento iraniano, durante o funeral do aiatolá Ali Khamenei, em Teerã, capital do Irã. — Foto: Majid Asgaripour/WANA/Reuters

Ainda sobre as parcerias econômicas com os vizinhos do Oriente Médio, neste sábado, a mídia estatal iraniana noticiou que Teerã concedeu permissão para que vários petroleiros do Iraque atravessem o Estreito de Ormuz.

A agência de notícias IRNA informou que a obtenção de uma autorização especial para as embarcações iraquianas foi um dos principais pedidos de Bagdá durante a visita de Ghalibaf ao Iraque.

Durante uma conferência, o presidente iraquiano, Nizar Amedi, confirmou que o Irã facilitou a passagem de navios transportando petróleo iraquiano pelo Estreito nos últimos dias, e que Bagdá discutiu a exportação de petróleo iraquiano através do Estreito de Ormuz com autoridades iranianas .

O Iraque está entre os países mais afetados pelo fechamento efetivo do Estreito de Ormuz pelo Irã . Antes do início da guerra, Bagdá produzia cerca de 4 milhões de barris de petróleo por dia.

A "operação econômica mais esmagadora" já realizada contra um país foi anunciada pelo presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, na quarta-feira (19).

Trump afirmou ainda esperar que todos os aliados dos Estados Unidos trabalhem para "isolar" e "derrotar" a "ameaça iraniana", e também ameaçou punir qualquer país que ajudar a manter a economia iraniana funcionando, sem detalhar qual seria a punição.

Um dia depois, na quinta-feira (20), o ministro das Relações Exteriores iraniano, Abbas Araqchi, disse que o "Dia D Econômico" dos EUA contra o Irã é apenas uma distração dos problemas econômicos americanos e alertou que a pressão adicional fracassaria, levando "mais derrota" aos Estados Unidos.

Quase seis meses após o início da guerra, a economia iraniana está sofrendo um duro golpe devido às sanções e ao bloqueio naval , que torna extremamente difícil para o país exportar petróleo, seu produto mais valioso. No entanto, como está está sujeito a sanções ocidentais há anos, o país se tornou-se hábil em contorná-las parcialmente.

“A capacidade de resistência do Irã não apenas evita o colapso, como também impede que o sofrimento econômico se traduza na pressão política e nas mudanças que os EUA esperam”, afirma Hadi Kahalzadeh, especialista em economia iraniana da Universidade Brandeis.

O Iraque está entre os países mais afetados pelo fechamento efetivo do Estreito de Ormuz pelo Irã . Antes do início da guerra, Bagdá produzia cerca de 4 milhões de barris de petróleo por dia.
A "operação econômica mais esmagadora" já realizada contra um país foi anunciada pelo presidente dos Estados Unidos, Donald Trump, na quarta-feira (19).

Trump afirmou ainda esperar que todos os aliados dos Estados Unidos trabalhem para "isolar" e "derrotar" a "ameaça iraniana", e também ameaçou punir qualquer país que ajudar a manter a economia iraniana funcionando, sem detalhar qual seria a punição.

Um dia depois, na quinta-feira (20), o ministro das Relações Exteriores iraniano, Abbas Araqchi, disse que o "Dia D Econômico" dos EUA contra o Irã é apenas uma distração dos problemas econômicos americanos e alertou que a pressão adicional fracassaria, levando "mais derrota" aos Estados Unidos.

Quase seis meses após o início da guerra, a economia iraniana está sofrendo um duro golpe devido às sanções e ao bloqueio naval , que torna extremamente difícil para o país exportar petróleo, seu produto mais valioso. No entanto, como está está sujeito a sanções ocidentais há anos, o país se tornou-se hábil em contorná-las parcialmente.

“A capacidade de resistência do Irã não apenas evita o colapso, como também impede que o sofrimento econômico se traduza na pressão política e nas mudanças que os EUA esperam”, afirma Hadi Kahalzadeh, especialista em economia iraniana da Universidade Brandeis.

articles.title: Como será o supercomputador brasileiro de IA com investimento de R$ 1 bilhão | G1
articles.standfirst: Plano do governo prevê que equipamento no Rio Grande do Norte comece a operar em 2027. Iniciativa com foco em inteligência artificial também prevê instalação de outra máquina no Rio de Janeiro em parceria com empresas chinesas.
articles.summary: Plano do governo prevê que equipamento no Rio Grande do Norte comece a operar em 2027. Iniciativa com foco em inteligência artificial também prevê instalação de outra máquina no Rio de Janeiro em parceria com empresas chinesas.
articles.body:
O Brasil deverá ter um novo supercomputador em operação a partir de 2027. O projeto anunciado na última quinta-feira (20) faz parte de um plano voltado à inteligência artificial e prevê um investimento de R$ 1,06 bilhão .

A máquina será comprada por meio de edital e ficará instalada no Parque Científico e Tecnológico Augusto Severo, em Macaíba (RN). Entre outras funções, servirá para criar e treinar modelos de IA .

🗒️ Tem alguma sugestão de reportagem? Envie para o g1

O governo apresentou ainda um projeto para instalar outro supercomputador no Rio de Janeiro, além de planos para criar um serviço brasileiro de armazenamento em nuvem e ampliar a fabricação local de chips. (saiba mais abaixo)

As iniciativas fazem parte do Plano Brasileiro de Inteligência Artificial (PBIA), lançado em 2024 e com previsão de R$ 23 bilhões em investimentos na área até 2028.

Data center da Meta em Indiana, nos Estados Unidos — Foto: Divulgação/Meta

Segundo o governo, a instalação de novos supercomputadores deve ampliar a capacidade de processamento de dados do país e estimular avanços em áreas como agricultura, indústria, saúde e prevenção de desastres climáticos.

A estrutura será voltada a empresas, universidades, instituições de pesquisa e órgãos públicos. A expectativa é que ajude a reduzir a dependência de empresas estrangeiras de processamento de dados.

O supercomputador que será instalado no Rio Grande do Norte terá capacidade de 7.200 petaflops .

🔎 Flop é a unidade usada para medir quantas operações matemáticas simples um computador consegue realizar por segundo.

A capacidade anunciada indica que o futuro equipamento será capaz de fazer, em um segundo, a mesma quantidade de cálculos que os 8 bilhões de habitantes da Terra levariam juntos cerca de 29 anos para completar.

Segundo o Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação, a máquina estará entre as dez mais potentes do mundo para processamento de inteligência artificial .

Ela será instalada no parque científico e tecnológico localizado na Universidade Federal do Rio Grande do Norte (UFRN). Segundo o governo, o estado foi escolhido por conta do potencial energético e da oportunidade de descentralizar a infraestrutura de alta tecnologia do país .

O segundo supercomputador será instalado no Rio de Janeiro , por meio de uma parceria entre a Rede Nacional de Ensino e Pesquisa (RNP) e as empresas chinesas de tecnologia Huawei e iFlyTek.

A estrutura deverá iniciar as operações em julho de 2027 e receber um investimento de R$ 1,276 bilhão durante cinco anos, de acordo com o Ministério da Ciência, Tecnologia e Inovação.

Ainda segundo a pasta, o equipamento será usado para criar um modelo brasileiro de linguagem semelhante aos usados por serviços como ChatGPT, em uma tentativa de permitir a criação de soluções de IA mais adequadas para o país.

O governo também anunciou o início da estruturação da Nuvem Brasileira, um serviço de armazenamento e processamento de dados em nuvem controlado pelo país e voltado para diminuir a dependência de provedores estrangeiros.

A proposta é criar uma solução com padrões abertos e interoperáveis para não focar em apenas uma empresa ou tecnologia. Segundo o governo, ela será desenvolvida em parceria com setores público e privado.

A Nuvem Brasileira será estruturada a partir de um acordo do Ministério da Gestão e da Inovação em Serviços Públicos com o Serpro e o BNDES. O mercado poderá opinar sobre a capacidade nacional de implementar a solução e sobre o modelo a ser seguido.

Supercomputador Santos Dumont, em Petrópolis (RJ) — Foto: Santos Dumont / Divulgação LNCC

Outra frente é uma iniciativa para ampliar a capacidade brasileira de produzir chips de inteligência artificial. Segundo o governo, trata-se de uma estratégia de longo prazo, com horizonte de 10 a 15 anos.

Para reduzir a dependência de tecnologias controladas por poucas empresas ou países, a iniciativa será baseada na arquitetura RISC-V, que define regras básicas para o funcionamento dos chips.

Por ser de código aberto, a RISC-V permite que empresas e instituições desenvolvam chips sem depender de uma tecnologia controlada por uma única companhia. A iniciativa será conduzida em cooperação com o ecossistema de inovação de Barcelona, na Espanha.

O governo federal anunciou ainda o plano de criar o Centro Nacional de Transparência Algorítmica e IA Confiável, um organismo voltado a monitorar o funcionamento dos sistemas de inteligência artificial e identificar eventuais riscos.

O órgão será estruturado pelo Centro de Pesquisa Aplicada em Inteligência Artificial da Universidade Federal de Minas Gerais (UFMG) e terá apenas funções técnicas. Não poderá, por exemplo, aplicar penalidades a empresas de IA.

Entre os objetivos do novo centro de IA estão o desenvolvimento de pesquisas, metodologias e ferramentas voltadas à transparência, à segurança e à redução de vieses em sistemas de inteligência artificial.

ChatGPT, DeepSeek, Claude, Mistral AI, Gemini, Copilot e Poe — Foto: Solen Feyissa/Unsplash

articles.title: Trump impõe tarifas de 50% ao Canadá após fracasso de negociações | G1
articles.standfirst: Medida entra em vigor neste sábado (22). Governo Trump afirma que Canadá rejeitou finalizar acordo comercial; primeiro-ministro Mark Carney diz que negociações não avançaram o suficiente para atender aos interesses do país.
articles.summary: Medida entra em vigor neste sábado. Governo Trump afirma que Canadá rejeitou finalizar acordo comercial; primeiro-ministro canadense diz que negociações não avançaram o suficiente.
articles.body:
Mark Carney, primeiro-ministro do Canadá, e Trump, presidente dos EUA — Foto: Reuters

Os Estados Unidos vão retomar, a partir deste sábado (22), tarifas de 50% sobre produtos importados do Canadá, após as negociações por um acordo entre os dois países falharem. As informações são da Reuters.

Segundo o governo do presidente Donald Trump, o governo canadense se recusou a finalizar um acordo que, na avaliação americana, teria reduzido substancialmente as tarifas e oferecido ao Canadá condições mais favoráveis de acesso ao mercado dos EUA.

As novas tarifas entraram em vigor à 0h01, no horário de Washington (1h01 no horário de Brasília). A medida foi anunciada por um alto funcionário do governo Trump, que também afirmou que não há novas reuniões de negociação previstas entre os dois países.

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, durante um evento para assinar uma ordem executiva sobre flexibilidade na vacinação em 10 de agosto de 2026 — Foto: Kylie Cooper/Reuters

O representante comercial dos Estados Unidos, Jamieson Greer, afirmou que o Canadá continua mantendo medidas de retaliação contra produtos americanos. Outro alto funcionário do governo Trump disse, porém, que os Estados Unidos não esperam uma nova retaliação canadense em resposta às tarifas de 50% que entram em vigor neste sábado.

O governo americano também afirma que a proposta oferecia condições favoráveis para as exportações canadenses de automóveis aos Estados Unidos. Segundo o funcionário, o Canadá, no entanto, queria mais concessões relacionadas às tarifas previstas na chamada Seção 232 da legislação comercial americana, que permite a aplicação de tarifas por motivos de segurança nacional.

Para o governo Trump, o objetivo das medidas é proteger empregos americanos, garantir as cadeias de abastecimento e estimular a transferência de produção industrial para os Estados Unidos. O funcionário afirmou ainda que o acordo em negociação teria tratado das tarifas de retaliação impostas anteriormente pelo Canadá.

O primeiro-ministro do Canadá, Mark Carney, participa de uma coletiva de imprensa para discutir uma resposta às novas tarifas do presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump, em Ottawa, Ontário, Canadá. — Foto: Blair Gable/ Reuters

O primeiro-ministro canadense, Mark Carney, anunciou que decidiu suspender as negociações comerciais com os Estados Unidos. Segundo ele, o progresso obtido nas conversas não foi suficiente para atender aos objetivos do Canadá.

Carney afirmou que, diante da imposição das tarifas de 50% pelos Estados Unidos, o Canadá vai responder com tarifas equivalentes, "dólar por dólar", para proteger trabalhadores e empresas do país.

A declaração contrasta com a avaliação do governo Trump de que as negociações estavam próximas de culminar em um acordo . Segundo o representante do governo americano, as reuniões entre as duas delegações foram "muito francas", mas não tiveram caráter hostil.

As tarifas anunciadas pelos Estados Unidos são aplicadas com base na Seção 338 da legislação comercial americana, segundo uma orientação da autoridade de Alfândega e Proteção de Fronteiras dos EUA.

articles.title: Chile fecha embaixada em Teerã em meio à escalada de tensões entre EUA e Irã | G1
articles.standfirst: Decisão ocorre após ambos os lados do conflito ameaçarem retaliar aliados. Em comunicado oficial, o governo do Chile esclarece que o encerramento das atividades diplomáticas na capital iraniana não representa a ruptura das relações.
articles.summary: Decisão ocorre após ambos os lados do conflito ameaçarem retaliar aliados. Em comunicado oficial, o governo do Chile esclarece que o encerramento das atividades diplomáticas na capital iraniana não representa a ruptura das relações.
articles.body:
Em comunicado oficial divulgado neste sábado (22), o Ministério das Relações Exteriores do Chile anunciou o encerramento das atividades da Embaixada chilena na República Islâmica do Irã . A medida entra em vigor no dia 31 de agosto e surge em um contexto de crescente instabilidade geopolítica no Oriente Médio.

A decisão chilena se insere em um cenário de escalada de tensões diplomáticas e militares entre os Estados Unidos e o Irã.

Na última quarta-feira (19), o presidente Donald Trump prometeu uma "guerra econômica" contra o país persa, afirmando que qualquer nação que permita que suas "instituições financeiras, empresas, aeroportos ou órgãos governamentais" forneçam apoio ao Irã enfrentará "consequências". Trump declarou ainda esperar que todos os aliados americanos se comprometam a "isolar" e "derrotar" o que chamou de "ameaça iraniana".

🔎 O presidente americano, no entanto, não detalhou como a ofensiva vai funcionar nem como pretende punir países que colaborarem com o Irã.

A resposta iraniana não tardou. Também neste sábado (22), a agência de notícias Iran International reportou que Mohsen Rezaei, secretário do Conselho Supremo de Segurança Nacional do Irã, ameaçou retaliar aliados dos Estados Unidos na região . Segundo a agência, Rezaei afirmou à mídia estatal ter advertido os países vizinhos a não se aliarem a Washington: "caso contrário, os consideraremos inimigos."

Ministério das Relações Exteriores do Chile anunciou o encerramento das atividades de sua Embaixada Teerã — Foto: Ministerio de Relaciones Exteriores de Chile

De acordo com a chancelaria chilena, o fechamento da embaixada em Teerã faz parte de uma "reorganização operacional" interna ao ministério, com o objetivo de redirecionar recursos para áreas prioritárias da "política externa do governo". O comunicado reconhece, porém, que os "fatores de segurança no Oriente Médio" também pesaram na deliberação, classificando a medida como de caráter preventivo.

🔎 Apesar do encerramento das operações em Teerã, o governo chileno é enfático ao afirmar que a decisão não representa uma ruptura diplomática entre os dois países.

Os serviços consulares anteriormente prestados pela embaixada na capital iraniana serão transferidos para o Consulado do Chile em Ancara, na Turquia, garantindo a continuidade do atendimento aos cidadãos que necessitem de assistência consular.

articles.title: Rússia acusa Ucrânia pela morte de 10 pessoas em ataques com drones | G1
articles.standfirst: Bombardeios ocorreram em diferentes regiões russas, após dois dias de grandes ofensivas russas ao território ucraniano.
articles.summary: Bombardeios ocorreram em diferentes regiões russas, após dois dias de grandes ofensivas russas ao território ucraniano.
articles.body:
Drones ucranianos mataram pelo menos 10 civis durante a noite desta sexta-feira (21) e a madrugada deste sábado (22) em uma onda de ataques contra a Rússia , segundo autoridades regionais do país.

Um dos bombardeios ocorreu em Samara. Em uma publicação no Telegram, o governador da região, Vyacheslav Fedorishchev, afirmou que uma idosa morreu e várias pessoas ficaram feridas depois que um armazém pertencente à varejista online Ozon e uma instalação industrial - que, de acordo com as Forças Armadas da Ucrânia , foi a refinaria de Novokuibyshevsk - foram atingidos.

➡️ Este é o primeiro ataque contra a Ozon, após semanas de ataques com drones contra sua concorrente maior, a Wildberries , que a Ucrânia classificou como parte de uma campanha mais ampla contra a infraestrutura econômica que sustenta a guerra russa na Ucrânia .

Coluna de fumaça sobe de armazém da varejista russa Ozon após ataque de drone ucraniano — Foto: Redes sociais via REUTERS

Em Krasnodar, no sul da Rússia , o governador Veniamin Kondratyev informou que duas crianças morreram e dois adultos ficaram feridos em um ataque à cidade portuária de Yeysk, no Mar de Azov.

Em Belgorod, que faz fronteira com a Ucrânia , duas pessoas morreram e 13 ficaram feridas.

Em Bryansk, outra região fronteiriça, quatro pessoas ficaram feridas.

Em Luhansk, uma província do leste da Ucrânia quase totalmente controlada pela Rússia , o governador Leonid Pasechnik, indicado por Moscou , afirmou que dois civis, incluindo um menino de 16 anos, foram mortos e outros nove ficaram feridos.

O Ministério da Defesa da Rússia afirmou ter abatido um total de 457 drones ucranianos durante a noite.

O presidente russo, Vladimir Putin, condenou os ataques e disse que Kiev , que alega ter como objetivo cortar o financiamento do esforço de guerra de Moscou , abriu uma "caixa de Pandora" de retaliação russa.

Nos dois dias anteriores foi a Ucrânia que acusou a Rússia de ataques com a morte de civis.

Na tarde desta sexta-feira (21), drones russos atingiram um movimentado shopping da cidade de Kryvyi Rih , no leste do país, deixando 15 mortos e quase uma centena de feridos.

Outro ataque de drones atingiu a cidade de Tokarivka, no sul da Ucrânia , e matou quatro pessoas, três delas crianças.

Interior de shopping destruído na Ucrânia após ataque russo — Foto: Procuradoria-Geral via Telegram/Divulgação via REUTERS

O presidente ucraniano chamou o bombardeio de "absolutamente cínico e desprezível" e voltou a pressionar os aliados, como fez no dia anterior, após uma imensa ofensiva russa contra Kiev .

"Ataques como esse são simplesmente atos de terrorismo. E o mundo precisa reagir de forma correspondente, exercendo pressão real sobre o agressor", cobrou.

Um dia antes, na madrugada de quinta-feira (20), um ataque da Rússia em larga escala à capital da Ucrânia , Kiev , e seu entorno matou 15 pessoas e atingiu uma escola, um hospital infantil, uma creche e pelo menos 30 edifícios.

Em post na rede social Telegram, Zelensky postou fotos de alguns dos alvos atingidos e lamentou a morte de civis no que classificou como "um dos mais cínicos e calculados" bombardeios russos.

O Ministério da Defesa russo confirmou o ataque, mas afirmou ter atingido instalações que produzem componentes para drones, um depósito militar e um centro de logística.

Bombeiro caminha por prédio de Kiev atingido por míssel balístico russo — Foto: Telegram / Reprodução

De acordo com o líder ucraniano, a Rússia usou diferentes tipos de mísseis e 168 drones em sua ofensiva, e boa parte foi interceptada pelas Forças Armadas do país . No entanto, Zelensky aproveitou para voltar a pressionar os aliados, os países europeus e os Estados Unidos, por sistemas de defesa antiaérea Patriot.

"A maior ameaça é a dos mísseis balísticos. E isso depende inteiramente do fornecimento de mísseis para os sistemas Patriot destinados à Ucrânia , o que significa que depende dos parceiros do nosso Estado. Não se pode simplesmente observar em silêncio, com indiferença e inação, enquanto os russos destroem vidas", criticou.

A presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen, respondeu a mensagem em um post na rede social X. Disse que estava trabalhando com os Estados-membros e parceiros para fornecer à Ucrânia recursos antibalísticos como "a mais urgente das prioridades".

Também nesta quinta, questionado sobre o possível andamento de negociações de paz, o Kremlin afirmou que não tem informações sobre uma visita dos negociadores americanos Steve Witkoff e Jared Kushner a Moscou , após o presidente da Ucrânia anunciar que entregou propostas para dar fim à guerra aos dois representantes dos EUA.

articles.title: As empresas onde os jovens sonham em trabalhar; veja ranking | G1
articles.standfirst: Estudo do CIEE mostra que 54% dos jovens consideram a possibilidade de crescer na carreira o principal fator para escolher onde trabalhar
articles.summary: Estudo do CIEE mostra que 54% dos jovens consideram a possibilidade de crescer na carreira o principal fator para escolher onde trabalhar
articles.body:
Pesquisa do CIEE e Instituto Locomotiva revela que jovens priorizam crescimento profissional ao escolher empresas para trabalhar — Foto: g1

Para os jovens brasileiros, o emprego dos sonhos vai além do salário. A oportunidade de crescer na carreira é o principal critério na escolha de uma empresa, e grandes marcas estão entre os lugares em que essa geração mais deseja trabalhar.

É o que aponta um levantamento do Centro de Integração Empresa-Escola (CIEE), realizado em parceria com o Instituto Locomotiva. O estudo ouviu 8.881 jovens de 14 a 24 anos de todas as regiões do país.

🗒️ Tem alguma sugestão de reportagem? Mande para o g1

Na categoria "Meu Match Perfeito", os primeiros colocados aparecem em situação de empate técnico. O ranking indica que a preferência da nova geração se concentra em grandes marcas e empresas já consolidadas no mercado.

A preferência por grandes empresas está alinhada a outro resultado da pesquisa: na hora de escolher onde trabalhar, os jovens valorizam mais as oportunidades de crescimento profissional do que a remuneração. Salário e benefícios aparecem em segundo lugar entre os critérios mais mencionados.

54%: oportunidade de crescimento profissional;

19%: estabilidade e segurança no emprego;

18%: identificação com valores e cultura organizacional;

18%: admiração pela marca ou pelos produtos.

O resultado mostra que o salário continua sendo importante, mas, sozinho, não é suficiente para definir onde os jovens desejam trabalhar. A possibilidade de aprender, se desenvolver e crescer profissionalmente surge como uma prioridade ainda maior.

Essa expectativa também aparece quando os entrevistados falam sobre o que esperam das empresas. Segundo a pesquisa, 98% consideram importante trabalhar em organizações que incentivem o crescimento profissional. O mesmo percentual afirma que é importante que os profissionais mais jovens sejam reconhecidos e valorizados.

A identificação com a empresa também influencia essa escolha. Cerca de sete em cada 10 jovens afirmam que não trabalhariam em organizações cujos valores e princípios sejam diferentes dos seus. O dado reforça a importância de aspectos como propósito, responsabilidade social e ambiente de trabalho na relação com o empregador.

Segundo a pesquisa, 98% consideram muito importante trabalhar em empresas que valorizem a saúde mental dos funcionários. A expectativa, portanto, envolve não apenas crescimento profissional, mas também qualidade de vida e boas condições de trabalho.

Ao mesmo tempo, o porte da empresa continua associado à segurança. Segundo a pesquisa, 90% dos entrevistados acreditam que trabalhar em uma grande companhia oferece mais estabilidade.

Centro de Integração Empresa-Escola (CIEE). Espírito Santo — Foto: Divulgação/CIEE

A pesquisa também revela outro aspecto da relação dos jovens com o mercado de trabalho: quais empresas mais abriram oportunidades para esse público no primeiro trimestre de 2026.

Os dados foram obtidos junto ao Ministério do Trabalho e Emprego (MTE) e incluem contratações pelo regime da CLT, vagas de aprendizagem e oportunidades de estágio.

Na contratação pela Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT), o Mercado Livre ficou na primeira posição do ranking nacional.

Na modalidade de aprendizagem, a liderança ficou com a Sendas Distribuidora S/A, responsável pelo Assaí Atacadista.

Ranking nacional de contratação de aprendizes

Sendas Distribuidora S/A (Assaí Atacadista)

Supermercados BH Comércio de Alimentos S/A

SPDM (Associação Paulista para o Desenvolvimento da Medicina)

Já no estágio, o setor público aparece com força. Tribunais de Justiça e órgãos governamentais ocupam boa parte das primeiras posições.

Ranking nacional de contratação de estagiários

Instituto Nacional do Seguro Social (INSS)

Defensoria Pública do Estado de São Paulo

Secretaria de Ciência, Tecnologia e Ensino Superior do Paraná

articles.title: Have You Experienced “Raise Shaming”? Here’s What It Can Look Like at Work
articles.summary: When asking for what you deserve in the office comes with a guilt trip.
articles.body:
When Emma, a project coordinator in Atlanta, found herself tasked with the responsibilities of her boss's job without any of the titles, recognition, or pay that came with it, she started preparing for her next salary negotiation. "I put together this whole proposal comparing market trends, the benefits I've given to the company since I joined, and the points I wanted to make to the director," she said, recounting best negotiation practices she'd learned from years of women in the workplace lunch-and-learns, best-selling business books, and Instagram motivation to 'just ask for more' and 'charge your worth'.

So when the director of her division responded by reminding Emma that she'd already agreed to a $43,000 annual salary when she accepted the job a year earlier, and suggested Emma move back in with her parents or get a second job if she needed to earn more money, she was shocked. "They made this one comment, 'It's like you're asking us to buy you a Louis Vuitton bag,' as if I was asking the company to pay for my life of luxury," said Emma. "I just wanted to be able to afford a dingy 700-square-foot apartment," she added. But her director doubled down: Shouldn't she just be happy with what she already had?

Related: Gen Z Is Making a Surprisingly Smart Retirement Move Right Now

Why Asking for More Can Come With Backlash

This pattern came up in dozens of interviews I conducted with women about their negotiation experiences—raise shaming: Women who spoke up, asked for more, and asserted their value only to be chastised, shamed, or even punished for doing so:

"We're not sure we want someone so money-motivated."

"You're asking for more money? We're a startup."

"It seems like this isn't a good fit for you and good luck finding something else."

For decades, popular career advice for women has rested on the assumption that gender pay gaps, promotion gaps, and leadership gaps were driven by women not negotiating enough. For women like Emma, who grew up on this advice only to find themselves judged, ridiculed, and penalized for asking for 'too much,' the experience can be disorienting, even demoralizing. "I was kind of shell-shocked. I was not expecting to be treated that way," said Emma. "It just made me feel completely devalued."

"Traditional [negotiation] advice assumes that the same words delivered the same way will be received the same way from everyone, and that's not the case," says Damali Peterman, attorney, negotiation expert, and author of Be Who You Are to Get What You Want. "A woman displaying the same behavior as a man could be described as aggressive, demanding, or difficult. A man doing the exact same thing can be described as confident, decisive, or leadership material," she says, pointing to a gendered double standard that not only leads to different perceptions but also to different outcomes.

"A woman displaying the same behavior as a man could be described as aggressive, demanding, or difficult. A man doing the exact same thing can be described as confident, decisive, or leadership material."

Damali Peterman, attorney, negotiation expert, and author

Researchers consistently find that when women express the assertiveness and ambition necessary to be seen as competent or to advance at work, they're not only perceived as less likable than their male peers, they're also perceived as less hireable . When women ask for more, they're not only more likely to be labeled aggressive and demanding, they're more likely than their male counterparts to experience penalties as a result. I interviewed women who were sidelined from future advancement or excluded from existing opportunities; some who even had job offers rescinded after asking for more.

"I think that we as a society have to stop pretending that the only thing that's standing between women and equitable compensation is a willingness to ask," says Peterman. Indeed, more recent research has revealed that women in the U.S. have been as likely to ask for raises and promotions as their male peers for decades , but the judgment levied against women who ask leaves them far less likely to get what they want when they do.

"When I started negotiating my salary, it was very clear that many of my male bosses specifically felt really uncomfortable about it," business journalist and author of Uncompete: Rejecting Competition to Unlock Success, Ruchika T. Malhotra, told me. "I had one male boss who said, 'Yes, you deserve it, but what will our other male reporters think?'"

Even after changing workplaces—a new job, a new manager, and in a new industry—the raise shaming continued. "The most egregious was when I negotiated my salary and my manager basically said that because your husband is in the technology industry (which is high paying), you don't need a raise," said Malhotra. "Hearing that was definitely a slap in the face."

While the message that you get what you ask for (or deserve) might seem empowering, Malhotra points out how it can actually work to disempower those most affected by this bias-driven backlash. "If you come in with this view that the world is meritocratic, like what matters is how good you are, how hard you work and nothing else, when you face this sort of backlash and bias, it can feel very difficult and emotionally unsettling," said Malhotra. "It could very much bring out those feelings of I don't belong here, I'm not good enough, all of that"—conditioning those who already face the most systematic discrimination (across gender identity as well as race, sexuality, ability, and other intersections of identity) to internalize it as a personal failure.

"If you come in with this view that the world is meritocratic, like what matters is how good you are, how hard you work and nothing else, when you face this sort of backlash and bias, it can feel very difficult and emotionally unsettling."

Ruchika T. Malhotra, journalist and author

"Financial shame is such a powerful and complicated thing because it can be something that you did, but it could also be something that happened to you," says Hanna Horvath, Certified Financial Planner and creator of the Your Brain on Money newsletter. "You can internalize that shame whether it's valid or not. And a lot of times it's not valid, and it changes the way that you approach your money and these kinds of decisions going forward," she adds.

Indeed, research affirms that women are given more negative evaluations, are considered less likable and are deemed less worthy of workplace opportunity when they self-promote, and it's this real increase in backlash (as opposed to a lack of confidence) that can keep them from self-promoting to the same extent in the future. In this way, the cost of raise shaming can compound, as those already most exposed to it modify their behavior to shield themselves against more of it.

What to Do If You Experience Raise Shaming

"It's really important that you don't confuse someone else's discomfort with your ambition as evidence that your request was unreasonable," says Peterman . In fact, she encourages women to continue asking for more with these biases in mind, instead of being blindsided by them. To do that, Peterman developed what she refers to as a RESET framework:

Regulate your immediate reaction and take the time to separate the emotional injury of being shamed or penalized from strategic decisions about what you should do next. "Whether it's disappointment, anger, or embarrassment—you should feel all those things," says Peterman. That said, she cautions against shame. "If you ask a legitimate question about compensation, that's not a character flaw," she says.

Examine what actually happened. What changed after the negotiation? Peterman points out that a rejected request for more is not the same thing as being shamed for asking in the first place. "If it's just a 'no,' maybe it's a 'no' to that specific ask," says Peterman, in which case, the rejection can be an opportunity to collect more information. "There's so many different ingredients that can go into that end result—reorganization, acquisition, or merger," in addition to bias, says Peterman. You may want to ask, " Can you help me understand the business reason for that decision?"

That said, if you get a "no" and suddenly find yourself uninvited to meetings, removed from projects, getting drastically different performance feedback and evaluations, excluded from previous advancement opportunities, characterized as difficult or aggressive or ungrateful, or experiencing major changes in bonuses or other compensation, you can use that information to substantiate your experience of backlash.

Save the record to create a factual timeline of what happened and document any specific changes (like those listed above). In addition to creating a contemporaneous record of events, Peterman says this process can help separate the immediate conclusions we come to in the aftermath of such shocks from the documented facts, which can lead to different determinations as we gather further insight or context.

Engage strategically to gather those additional insights, considering who may offer the best and the safest sources of information. It might be a supervisor with whom you have a good relationship, a mentor who you trust, or someone in HR who can offer a more neutral perspective or more insight into what actually drives pay and promotion decisions across the organization.

Take back your power. "It might be to negotiate in a different way or negotiate a more defined path forward. It might be to try to repair the relationship or a misconception. It may be to think about a different workplace that better recognizes that woman negotiator's value," says Peterman.

Peterman also encourages taking back your power in ways that extend beyond the specifics of any one negotiation, like sharing your experience with others, taking classes, or even creating art or pursuing other totally unrelated ventures. "Every time I meet someone who's had a setback, I encourage them to find a way to use that to bounce back so it doesn't have to be a permanent setback," she says.

"Every time I meet someone who's had a setback, I encourage them to find a way to use that to bounce back so it doesn't have to be a permanent setback."

"Strength in numbers is super important," says Malhotra, speaking to the ways in which taking back power and even shifting systems of power in and of themselves can often best be realized collectively rather than individually. "Some of the strongest changes come through solidarity, gathering with other employees, maybe even leveraging ERGs as a place to push for change," she says.

But even at the individual level, Malhotra advocates for building your own personal "board of directors" or "team of champions" that can both cheer you on and provide critical support in the face of workplace cultures that continue to subject some to far more of this backlash than others. This can advance the collective conversation that liberates more of us from internalizing this systemic bias as a personal failure, and puts the shame where it really belongs—on the organizations and institutions that continue to engage in it.

Related: It's 2026—So Why Is Talking About Money Still So Taboo?

Read the original article on Real Simple

"I just wanted to be able to afford a dingy 700-square-foot apartment," she added. But her director doubled down: Shouldn't she just be happy with what she already had?
Related: Gen Z Is Making a Surprisingly Smart Retirement Move Right Now
Why Asking for More Can Come With Backlash

This pattern came up in dozens of interviews I conducted with women about their negotiation experiences—raise shaming: Women who spoke up, asked for more, and asserted their value only to be chastised, shamed, or even punished for doing so:
"We're not sure we want someone so money-motivated."
"You're asking for more money? We're a startup."
"It seems like this isn't a good fit for you and good luck finding something else."

For decades, popular career advice for women has rested on the assumption that gender pay gaps, promotion gaps, and leadership gaps were driven by women not negotiating enough. For women like Emma, who grew up on this advice only to find themselves judged, ridiculed, and penalized for asking for 'too much,' the experience can be disorienting, even demoralizing. "I was kind of shell-shocked. I was not expecting to be treated that way," said Emma. "It just made me feel completely devalued."

"Traditional [negotiation] advice assumes that the same words delivered the same way will be received the same way from everyone, and that's not the case," says Damali Peterman, attorney, negotiation expert, and author of Be Who You Are to Get What You Want. "A woman displaying the same behavior as a man could be described as aggressive, demanding, or difficult. A man doing the exact same thing can be described as confident, decisive, or leadership material," she says, pointing to a gendered double standard that not only leads to different perceptions but also to different outcomes.

"A woman displaying the same behavior as a man could be described as aggressive, demanding, or difficult. A man doing the exact same thing can be described as confident, decisive, or leadership material."
Damali Peterman, attorney, negotiation expert, and author

Researchers consistently find that when women express the assertiveness and ambition necessary to be seen as competent or to advance at work, they're not only perceived as less likable than their male peers, they're also perceived as less hireable . When women ask for more, they're not only more likely to be labeled aggressive and demanding, they're more likely than their male counterparts to experience penalties as a result. I interviewed women who were sidelined from future advancement or excluded from existing opportunities; some who even had job offers rescinded after asking for more.

"I think that we as a society have to stop pretending that the only thing that's standing between women and equitable compensation is a willingness to ask," says Peterman. Indeed, more recent research has revealed that women in the U.S. have been as likely to ask for raises and promotions as their male peers for decades , but the judgment levied against women who ask leaves them far less likely to get what they want when they do.

"When I started negotiating my salary, it was very clear that many of my male bosses specifically felt really uncomfortable about it," business journalist and author of Uncompete: Rejecting Competition to Unlock Success, Ruchika T. Malhotra, told me. "I had one male boss who said, 'Yes, you deserve it, but what will our other male reporters think?'"

Even after changing workplaces—a new job, a new manager, and in a new industry—the raise shaming continued. "The most egregious was when I negotiated my salary and my manager basically said that because your husband is in the technology industry (which is high paying), you don't need a raise," said Malhotra. "Hearing that was definitely a slap in the face."

While the message that you get what you ask for (or deserve) might seem empowering, Malhotra points out how it can actually work to disempower those most affected by this bias-driven backlash. "If you come in with this view that the world is meritocratic, like what matters is how good you are, how hard you work and nothing else, when you face this sort of backlash and bias, it can feel very difficult and emotionally unsettling," said Malhotra. "It could very much bring out those feelings of I don't belong here, I'm not good enough, all of that"—conditioning those who already face the most systematic discrimination (across gender identity as well as race, sexuality, ability, and other intersections of identity) to internalize it as a personal failure.

"If you come in with this view that the world is meritocratic, like what matters is how good you are, how hard you work and nothing else, when you face this sort of backlash and bias, it can feel very difficult and emotionally unsettling."
Ruchika T. Malhotra, journalist and author

"Financial shame is such a powerful and complicated thing because it can be something that you did, but it could also be something that happened to you," says Hanna Horvath, Certified Financial Planner and creator of the Your Brain on Money newsletter. "You can internalize that shame whether it's valid or not. And a lot of times it's not valid, and it changes the way that you approach your money and these kinds of decisions going forward," she adds.

Indeed, research affirms that women are given more negative evaluations, are considered less likable and are deemed less worthy of workplace opportunity when they self-promote, and it's this real increase in backlash (as opposed to a lack of confidence) that can keep them from self-promoting to the same extent in the future. In this way, the cost of raise shaming can compound, as those already most exposed to it modify their behavior to shield themselves against more of it.
What to Do If You Experience Raise Shaming

"It's really important that you don't confuse someone else's discomfort with your ambition as evidence that your request was unreasonable," says Peterman . In fact, she encourages women to continue asking for more with these biases in mind, instead of being blindsided by them. To do that, Peterman developed what she refers to as a RESET framework:

Regulate your immediate reaction and take the time to separate the emotional injury of being shamed or penalized from strategic decisions about what you should do next. "Whether it's disappointment, anger, or embarrassment—you should feel all those things," says Peterman. That said, she cautions against shame. "If you ask a legitimate question about compensation, that's not a character flaw," she says.

Examine what actually happened. What changed after the negotiation? Peterman points out that a rejected request for more is not the same thing as being shamed for asking in the first place. "If it's just a 'no,' maybe it's a 'no' to that specific ask," says Peterman, in which case, the rejection can be an opportunity to collect more information. "There's so many different ingredients that can go into that end result—reorganization, acquisition, or merger," in addition to bias, says Peterman. You may want to ask, " Can you help me understand the business reason for that decision?"

That said, if you get a "no" and suddenly find yourself uninvited to meetings, removed from projects, getting drastically different performance feedback and evaluations, excluded from previous advancement opportunities, characterized as difficult or aggressive or ungrateful, or experiencing major changes in bonuses or other compensation, you can use that information to substantiate your experience of backlash.

Save the record to create a factual timeline of what happened and document any specific changes (like those listed above). In addition to creating a contemporaneous record of events, Peterman says this process can help separate the immediate conclusions we come to in the aftermath of such shocks from the documented facts, which can lead to different determinations as we gather further insight or context.

Engage strategically to gather those additional insights, considering who may offer the best and the safest sources of information. It might be a supervisor with whom you have a good relationship, a mentor who you trust, or someone in HR who can offer a more neutral perspective or more insight into what actually drives pay and promotion decisions across the organization.

Take back your power. "It might be to negotiate in a different way or negotiate a more defined path forward. It might be to try to repair the relationship or a misconception. It may be to think about a different workplace that better recognizes that woman negotiator's value," says Peterman.

Peterman also encourages taking back your power in ways that extend beyond the specifics of any one negotiation, like sharing your experience with others, taking classes, or even creating art or pursuing other totally unrelated ventures. "Every time I meet someone who's had a setback, I encourage them to find a way to use that to bounce back so it doesn't have to be a permanent setback," she says.
"Every time I meet someone who's had a setback, I encourage them to find a way to use that to bounce back so it doesn't have to be a permanent setback."

"Strength in numbers is super important," says Malhotra, speaking to the ways in which taking back power and even shifting systems of power in and of themselves can often best be realized collectively rather than individually. "Some of the strongest changes come through solidarity, gathering with other employees, maybe even leveraging ERGs as a place to push for change," she says.

But even at the individual level, Malhotra advocates for building your own personal "board of directors" or "team of champions" that can both cheer you on and provide critical support in the face of workplace cultures that continue to subject some to far more of this backlash than others. This can advance the collective conversation that liberates more of us from internalizing this systemic bias as a personal failure, and puts the shame where it really belongs—on the organizations and institutions that continue to engage in it.
Related: It's 2026—So Why Is Talking About Money Still So Taboo?

articles.title: This El Niño could become 'the largest in living memory', forecasters warn. Americans could feel the effects into 2027.
articles.summary: El Niño's effect will be felt in 2027, making it 'very likely' to replace 2024 as the warmest year on record globally.
articles.body:
The El Niño developing over the Pacific Ocean could be "the largest in living memory," according to the Met Office , the U.K.'s national weather service.

The climate phenomenon, which the Met Office is calling "unprecedented," can boost global temperatures and increase the likelihood of extreme weather. Forecasters said it's likely to become the largest of its kind since the 19th century, adding that 2027 is very likely to replace 2024 as the warmest year on record globally.

El Niño is a periodic warming of sea surface temperatures in the eastern Pacific caused by weakening trade winds. It occurs naturally every two to seven years and tends to last between nine and 12 months.

The Met Office's latest forecasts show a rise of more than 5.4°F (3°C) in equatorial Pacific sea-surface temperatures later this year. A typical El Niño brings warming of 1.8°F to 3.6°F (1°C to 2°C), with 3.6°F (2°C) considered a major event.

"I have never seen a forecast that looks like this," Adam Scaife, a professor at the Met Office, told ITN News . "The strength of El Niño in our forecasts is already at very high levels, even at this early stage.

"It peaks in November, December, and by that stage, it looks very much like it's going to be a record event, the biggest in recent history, the biggest in living memory, and perhaps even the biggest for over a century."

The forecast is consistent with warnings from U.S. forecasters that a historically significant El Niño may be looming. Berkeley Earth , a nonprofit climate research group, found in July that there is a 90% chance tropical Pacific temperatures will exceed all records over about 150 years of observations. The National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration's Climate Prediction Center told Yahoo News it has classified the 2026 El Niño as ranking "among the largest El Niño events."

The Climate Prediction Center puts the odds at 69% that the event exceeds every El Niño measured since 1950 during the October-through-December stretch, and above 90% that it reaches "very strong" strength this fall and winter. The agency gives it a 97% chance of lasting into early spring 2027.

NOAA's outlook for December through February already shows a clear pattern taking shape, with the impacts of El Niño expected to become more pronounced as winter progresses.

"For the U.S., the impacts of El Niño are most clearly evident from fall through spring," Michelle L'Heureux, a physical scientist at NOAA's Climate Prediction Center, told Yahoo News.

"Generally speaking, El Niño tends to increase the storm track over the southern tier of the United States, increasing the chances of above-average precipitation," she added. "At the same time, because the storm track is shifted southward over the U.S., regions across the northern U.S. tend to be drier. The northern U.S. has the highest chances for above-average temperatures, too."

As it strengthens, El Niño's effects are expected to become increasingly apparent around the world — including in the U.S. Forecasters have predicted that warm summer temperatures, including the hottest July on record , may persist for longer than usual .

Parts of the Northeast were still experiencing hot and humid conditions this week as severe weather swept through the region. On Thursday, storms tore through a beach on Long Island, stranded dozens of people in cars in New Jersey and knocked out power in parts of Delaware's capital, the Associated Press reported.

Mike Lichniak, chief meteorologist at Delaware-area TV station WBOC , warned earlier that morning that rising humidity would push temperatures into the 80s and 90s, with a heat index above 100°F in some areas. Severe thunderstorms and an isolated tornado followed that afternoon and evening.

In NOAA's Climate Prediction Center seasonal temperature outlook for fall 2026, released on Aug. 20, the agency favors above-normal temperatures across nearly the entire country from September through November. The Pacific Northwest, the northern Rockies and parts of coastal Alaska have the highest odds, at 50% to 70%, of a warmer-than-normal season.

Much of the rest of the U.S., including the South, Midwest, Northeast and Florida, also has elevated odds of above-normal temperatures, at 33% to 50%.

The lone exception is a pocket of the Ohio Valley, covering parts of Illinois, Indiana, Kentucky and Missouri, where forecasters see "equal chances" of above-, near- or below-normal temperatures. No part of the country is expected to see a cooler-than-average fall.

The Climate Prediction Center's December-through-February outlook puts the wettest odds over Southern California, the southern tier and much of the East Coast, with its strongest confidence in the Southeast. The drier signal is confined to the northern tier, where the agency also expects above-normal temperatures.

That leaves the northern U.S. warm and dry, which is not the combination that produces heavy snow. The southern storm track can bring it instead to places that rarely get much.
