articles.title: Ghaziabad robbery: 2 held after gunfight, Rs 5 lakh of looted Rs 25 lakh recovered
articles.summary: GHAZIABAD: Ghaziabad police arrested two people for allegedly robbing Rs 25 lakh from a Meerut-based businessman on the Delhi-Meerut Expressway under .
articles.body: GHAZIABAD: Ghaziabad police arrested two people for allegedly robbing Rs 25 lakh from a Meerut-based businessman on the Delhi-Meerut Expressway under the jurisdiction of Wave City police station.The arrests were made after a gunfight in which both accused received bullet wounds in their legs.According to police, the accused were identified as Saddam (20), a resident of Arthala, Sahibabad of Ghaziabad and Aasif (38), a resident of Meerut.A businessman carrying Rs 25 lakh in a bag was stopped right in the middle of Delhi-Meerut Expressway by armed men who blocked his Thar with two cars, held a pistol to his head and fled with the cashThe robbery took place around 7pm on Friday, when traffic continued to pass around the vehicle, oblivious to the crime the gang carried out inside the Thar.Gillaman, a Meerut businessman who owns a factory recycling waste material, was driving to Jafrabad in Delhi with his cousin Samad and relative Saleem to pay for supplies. He left Meerut around 5pm and reached Dasna in a couple of hours, when he was stopped on the expressway.Police registered an FIR against unknown persons under the section of 309 (4) (robbery) of BNS in Wave City police station.Priyashri Pal, ACP of Wave City said that on Tuesday early hours, the SWAT team and Crime Branch received information from an informer that the accused wanted in Case of a robbery of Rs 25 lakhs with Meerut based businessman on Delhi-Meerut Expressway, were roaming in the area on a Splendor motorcycle. On the information, the SWAT team, Crime Branch, SWAT team Nagar Zone, and Police Station Wave City police team started checking in the Wave City area.âDuring checking, 02 persons riding on one Splendor motorcycle without number plate were seen coming. When the police team tried to stop them, both motorcycle-borne persons, seeing the police checking and being surrounded by the police team, turned the motorcycle around and started fleeing back. When the police team chased them, they abandoned the motorcycle and started firing at the police team with the intention to kill. In retaliatory action, in the police encounter, both fleeing persons were injured after being shot in the leg and fell down. They were immediately sent to the hospital for treatment and their condition is stable,â she said.From the possession of the accused, the looted Rs 05 lakh was recovered along with 02 illegal country-made pistols of 0.315 bore, 04 live cartridges, 04 empty cartridges and a Splendor motorcycle without number plate were recovered.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Ghaziabad | Silver Rate in Ghaziabad | Bank Holidays in Ghaziabad | Public Holidays in Ghaziabad | Ghaziabad AQI | Weather in Ghaziabad | Petrol Price in Ghaziabad | Diesel Price in Ghaziabad | CNG Price in Ghaziabad | LPG Price in GhaziabadStay updated with the latest Ghaziabad news. articles.title: Somerset cider makers left with very few apples after heatwaves
articles.summary: Some orchards are harvesting just a 10th of their usual crop, and facing an uncertain future.
articles.body:
Somerset's famous cider orchards have been "decimated" by the long summer drought, producers say. Many trees have produced no fruit at all, and others have dropped their fruit early, rotting before they ripened.

"It's gut-wrenching," says Kimberly Jones of Honey's Cider near Bath, whose orchard has produced only a 10th of its normal amount of apples.

Neil MacDonald, who manages more than 1,000 acres of Somerset orchards, says he has watched half his apples fall before they have ripened, because the trees are stressed by the drought.

"Nothing sells cider like sunshine," he says, "and we've emptied our tanks.

"The sadness is we haven't got enough fruit to refill the tanks again."

Walking through Kimberly Jones' orchard just outside Bath, it's hard to see any apples at all. The trees should be groaning with fruit, she tells me, but "we might get 10% of our normal crop here, and that's generous".

The orchard is 25 years old, and this is by far the driest year they have had. Because 2025 was also dry, the trees became stressed, she explained, and this year most have just not made fruit at all, to save their energy.

Unlike the big commercial brands, Honey's Cider is only made from fresh juice. Jones refuses to buy apple concentrate or industrial products.

"So we can only make cider from the juice we make each year, which means we will be down this year," she adds.

Ironically, the long hot summer has been "brilliant" for actually selling cider.

"Everyone likes a cold cider on a hot day, but we are struggling now to grow fruit for next year," Jones says.

On one of Somerset's most famous cider farms, I hear the same story. Gordon Rich started pressing apples on a farm near Highbridge in 1954. Today his grandson George Scott makes nearly a million litres of cider a year.

"We would normally harvest 20-30 tonnes of apples here," he tells me, walking through one orchard.

"There's so little fruit in here I won't even put the harvester in - the sheep can have any that drop."

Neighbouring farms that Scott buys from are also short of fruit. One grower who normally produces 200 tonnes is "down to about 30", he adds.

Will his tanks run dry then, I wondered?

"No, we've got plenty of cider in the tanks for now," he smiles. Cider makers can keep stock from year to year, but Scott says he worries about the future of his trees.

Two years of drought have already stressed them, and climate scientists are warning farmers to expect more hot dry summers .

"I do worry that next year will show a lot more signs of the drought and the trees will be stressed again. If we get another dry year, I don't know what we're going to do," he adds.

Not every orchard is bare, of course. Neil MacDonald manages more than 1,000 acres of cider orchards across Somerset. At his Orchard Park Farm, near Shepton Mallet, I see plenty of apples - both on the trees and on the ground.

With a roar, the apple harvester starts up. It powers down the rows, sweeping up the apples under the trees, up and away into the trailer.

This is at least three weeks' early for harvest, but they are not picking up the fruit to make cider.

"All these apples will go on the compost heap," MacDonald tells me, ruefully.

He cuts one open to show me the inside, mottled brown and floury.

"It's unripe, but it's already rotted before we've even started," he explains.

"The trees are stressed without any water, so they've just dumped the fruit on the ground to save themselves."

The harvester sweeps along, filling a large trailer with cider apples that Neil and his team have spent all year trying to grow, only to throw away.

"We've probably lost about half the crop this way," he says.

"This should be a 20-tonne orchard. If I get 10 tonnes from it I'll be grateful."

Somerset's cider apple growers know this is not a freak year.

"What we used to think of as extreme weather, we increasingly consider as normal." says Mike Kendon, a climate scientist at the Met Office .

But what can an apple grower do about it?

Neil MacDonald is now watering newly planted trees.

"Five years ago you would just dig a good hole and leave nature to get on with it," he smiles.

"Now you can't get away with that, you have to irrigate young trees or they die."

But irrigation for hundreds of acres of cider orchards is "just not viable", he said. Farmers who grow eating apples for supermarkets command higher prices for their fruit, so traditionally they have invested in irrigation systems.

Cider growers are now having to rethink their calculations.

Most fundamentally of all, climate change may actually change the taste of West Country cider.

One of the main varieties that gives Somerset cider its bittersweet taste is Dabinett. Several growers have found these trees producing very few apples this year, not because of the drought, but the mild winter.

"Dabinett needs a cold snap," MacDonald explains. "We just didn't get the cold winter days this year or last, so it's not producing."

He is now grafting other varieties onto his Dabinett trees, plants that fare better in hot dry weather.

As our climate changes, the very taste of Somerset cider may change too.

articles.title: Mojtaba Khamenei seen, heard in rare video amid health concerns
articles.summary: Middle East News: A new video of Iranâs Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has surfaced amid growing mystery over his health, appearance and whereabouts.According to Al Ar.
articles.body: A new video of Iranâs Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei has surfaced amid growing mystery over his health, appearance and whereabouts.According to Al Arabiya, Iranâs Fars News released archival footage showing Mojtaba Khamenei surrounded by a group of people who offered prayers before beginning their discussions.The footage comes amid repeated claims by US President Donald Trump that Mojtaba is in "bad shape" and was "seriously injured" following the strikes that killed his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, Iranâs longest-serving Supreme Leader.This is the second video of Mojtaba Khamenei to emerge in August. The footage, however, is undated.It is also the first video in which his voice can be clearly heard. The video showed Mojtaba presiding religious academic discussion with clerics.The video was first published by Mehr, a semi-official Iranian news agency sponsored by the government and run by the Islamic Development Organisation. Its release appeared aimed at countering growing speculation about Mojtabaâs health and whereabouts.Reports of âextremely criticalâ conditionThe video surfaced after reports in Israeli media claimed that Mojtaba Khamenei was in an "extremely critical condition".Israelâs Channel 14, citing sources inside Iran, and an earlier report by The Jerusalem Post, quoting IranWire and sources close to Iranian President Masoud Pezeshkianâs administration, said concerns about Mojtabaâs health were circulating within Iranâs leadership.Iranian officials have rejected the reports.President Masoud Pezeshkian said Mojtaba Khamenei was "completely healthy", dismissing speculation about his physical condition, according to Iranâs ISNA news agency."Someone who can sit and discuss for seven to eight hours cannot have any health problems," Pezeshkian said, adding that he had held a "very good" meeting with Mojtaba earlier in August.Mojtabaâs low public profileMojtaba Khamenei became Iranâs Supreme Leader after his father Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, was killed in joint US-Israeli military strikes on February 28.Since taking over, Mojtaba has largely remained out of public view.Unlike previous Iranian leaders, he has not made public appearances and has communicated mainly through written statements.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: US removes Syria from terrorism list after 46 years - what it means for the Middle East country
articles.summary: US News: The United States on Monday removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism, ending a designation that had been in place since 1979 and imp.
articles.body: The United States on Monday removed Syria from its list of state sponsors of terrorism, ending a designation that had been in place since 1979 and imposing significant restrictions on trade, investment and financial transactions with the country.The move, which followed a 45-day congressional review, marks a further step in Washingtonâs efforts to deepen ties with Syriaâs new government under President Ahmed al-Sharaa. The US also revoked the designation of the Nusrah Front, later known as Hayâat Tahrir al-Sham (HTS), as a Specially Designated Global Terrorist organisation. The Treasury Department announced corresponding sanctions relief.âThese actions were all taken in recognition of the positive actions taken and further commitments by the Syrian government under President Ahmed al-Sharaa to fully distance Syria from acts of international terrorism,â US Secretary of State Marco Rubio said in a statement.Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the measures would encourage investment and support Syriaâs economic recovery. âToday's action will help foster additional investment in Syria to promote political and economic stability,â he said.The Treasury said the changes were âin line with President (Donald) Trump's promise to deliver sanctions relief to Syriaâ. It added that the removal of the restrictions âdoes not change Treasury's posture with regards to countering global terrorism and our commitment to hold bad actors in Syria accountable.âThe state sponsor designation had remained a major obstacle for businesses and financial institutions considering investment in Syria, even after the US ended its broader sanctions programme against the country in July 2025. The designation restricted US foreign assistance, defence exports and sales, certain dual-use goods and financial transactions.The Treasury has since said US financial institutions can provide services to Syria, process payments involving Syrian banks and establish correspondent banking relationships, provided sanctioned entities are not involved.Syriaâs government welcomed Mondayâs decision, describing it as an opportunity to reconnect with the global financial system and attract investment needed for reconstruction after nearly 14 years of war.Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad al-Shibani had earlier called the terrorism designation the âlast obstacleâ to rebuilding economic ties. âThere is no longer any obstacle to investment, doing business and rebuilding economic life in Syria,â he said.The US designation had been imposed in 1979, when Washington accused the government of then-President Hafez al-Assad of supporting militant groups. It continued under his son Bashar al-Assad, who was overthrown by rebels led by Sharaa in December 2024.HTS, formerly known as the Nusrah Front, was once affiliated with al Qaeda in Syria before breaking ties with the group in 2016. Sharaa later led the rebel coalition that toppled Assad and became president.With Syriaâs removal, Cuba, Iran and North Korea remain the three countries on the US state sponsors of terrorism list.The latest decision follows a broader rapprochement between Washington and Damascus. US President Donald Trump has backed sanctions relief for Syria and met Sharaa during a visit to Turkey, as the new Syrian government seeks international support for economic reconstruction.Syrian officials have also been pursuing closer links with international financial institutions and companies. The country's finance ministry has held discussions with Bank of America executives, while Mastercard has announced work with QNB Group and Syriaâs central bank to develop infrastructure for international card payments.Washington has said its engagement with Damascus is aimed at supporting Syriaâs stabilisation, economic recovery and reintegration into the global economy, while maintaining targeted measures against terrorism and other sanctioned actors.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Ghost in PM office? When cockroaches left Japan's Sanae Takaichi screaming
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said she has not encountered any ghosts at the official residence, but recently found herself unable to kill a .
articles.body: Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi said she has not encountered any ghosts at the official residence, but recently found herself unable to kill a cockroach that appeared there. She linked her hesitation to ideas about reincarnation that have stayed with her since childhood.She recounted the episode on X while answering a question she said she often receives about whether she has encountered ghosts at the residence. âIâve never encountered a ghost, but until recently, I was the one screaming when I came across cockroaches,â she wrote.âFirebirdâ shaped her responseTakaichi said she has read Osamu Tezukaâs Firebird repeatedly since childhood and that its depiction of reincarnation made a deep impression on her. The idea that âlife is connected, changing formsâ stayed with her as she grew older.She said that may be why she still cannot bring herself to kill insects, including cockroaches. When one appeared at the official residence, she recalled thinking: âMaybe this life is also part of that long cycle of reincarnation.âInstead of killing it, she left the cockroach alone for a while and hoped it would eventually make its own way out.Cockroach appeared despite precautionsHer previous accommodation, the membersâ dormitory, had never presented the same problem, she said. After moving into the official residence, she took several precautions to keep the place clean.She dealt carefully with food waste, cleaned around the dining area and washed used plastic containers. Even so, she was startled when a cockroach suddenly appeared near her feet.For some time, she kept the problem to herself and waited for the insect to leave. When she eventually told her secretaries what she had been doing, they were appalled.âOperation Combatâ ended sightingsâItâs unclean. Iâll handle it,â she quoted one of her secretaries as saying. The secretary then arranged what she called âOperation Combatâ.The measures worked, and she said there were no further cockroach sightings. Her reaction, however, was not entirely one of relief: âI felt relieved, but also a little lonely, or maybe sadâ¦â she wrote.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: CIA chief travels to Moscow for unannounced talks, US media reports
articles.summary: Flight tracking data confirms an American military aircraft travelled to Russia from the US via Latvia on Tuesday.
articles.body:
The head of the US Central Intelligence Agency (CIA) has travelled to Moscow for unannounced talks, the BBC's US news partner CBS has reported.

John Ratcliffe reportedly arrived in the Russian capital earlier on Tuesday. Neither Washington or Moscow have confirmed the nature of the visit or who he was due to meet.

In-person talks between high-level American and Russian officials are rare.

Flight tracking data confirmed a large US military aircraft travelled to Russia from the US via Latvia on Tuesday. It departed later on Tuesday.

BBC News has contacted the CIA, the White House and Pentagon for comment.

Footage posted on social media showed the C-17 transport plane approaching Moscow's Vnukovo international airport.

It departed Riga airport at 05:50 GMT and appeared to have landed in the Russian capital at around 07:04 GMT, according to data from FlightRadar24. It returned to Riga shortly before 17:00 GMT.

Footage on social media also purported to show a diplomatic motorcade travelling through Moscow.

Ahead of the trip, the US told Ukraine that a senior delegation would be travelling to Moscow and asked Kyiv to suspend strikes until they had left, a senior Ukrainian official told CBS.

The trip is thought to be Ratcliffe's first trip to Russia as CIA director, although he has maintained contact with his intelligence counterparts in Moscow.

John Foreman, who served as a British military attaché to Moscow between 2019 and 2022, told Radio 4's PM programme that the visit could be focused on "escalation management" given speculation recent drone activity in Germany could be linked to Russia .

He said: "The Americans don't normally send such a high ranking official to Moscow unannounced at short notice unless something is up."

Foreman said the trip could also concern the release of US detainees currently being held in Russia.

Ratcliffe played a role in negotiations for the release of Russian-American citizen Ksenia Karelina, who was jailed in Russia for over a year after being accused of providing support to Ukraine.

The CIA was also involved in a 2024 prisoner swap deal with Russia that saw the release of Wall Street Journal reporter Evan Gershkovich, as well as former US marine Paul Whelan and Russian-American journalist Alsu Kurmasheva.

The US has had strained relations with Russia since it launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022. Since then, Russia has been isolated on the world stage and faced international economic sanctions.

Ratcliffe appears to be one of the highest-ranking US officials to visit the country during President Donald Trump's second term.

Trump met Russian President Vladimir Putin at a summit in Alaska last year but the meeting did not lead to a breakthrough. Subsequent US-led peace talks between Russia and Ukraine appear to have stalled.

Additional reporting by Washington correspondent Daniel Bush and BBC Verify

articles.title: The $20,000 dorm room has arrived. Why Gen Z is taking its home away from home so seriously.
articles.summary: TikTok loves the monograms and custom decor. Students say the real appeal is having a tiny corner of campus that feels like theirs.
articles.body:
For Julie Beth Fox and Kari Cabale, designing the perfect dorms for their newly minted college freshmen was an act of love.

The two stay-at-home moms from Nashville first met when their kids, now in their 20s, were in kindergarten. They became fast friends, going to church together and supporting one another as they raised their combined six children. After years of coming up with fun and easy crafts and designing decor for various high school events, they were eager to flex their creativity to make their kids' rooms perfect, but within reason.

"I wanted her to be confident, and have all the things," Fox tells me of her oldest daughter, who attended Mississippi State. "But I also knew that I was going to set the precedent with her, and if I blew the budget, I would have to continue that. I spent a lot of time thinking it can be elegant, it can be elevated, but it doesn't have to be expensive."

The friends began helping out other moms in their community who found the process of outfitting a dorm room a bit overwhelming, and they loved it so much they decided to start their own company, which they named Petal and Pine Dorm Design . They weren't sure what to expect when they officially launched in June, but the response and the number of clients they have worked with have been beyond their wildest expectations.

"We're kind of overwhelmed and blown away, to be honest," Fox says. "We just thought we'd throw it out there, and we were quite surprised."

Their success is likely due to the fact that dorm design, as a concept, has gone viral. Gone are the days when you'd roll up at your first college living space with an extra-large twin "bed in a box" from Bed, Bath & Beyond and maybe a cute lamp or a poster and call it a day. Now, a perfectly aesthetic, curated dorm can take weeks or even months to create. Some students go all out, spending big bucks to make it perfect.

Beautifully decorated dorms have been trending on social media, particularly TikTok, for a few years, but this year they've hit the cultural zeitgeist in a new way. After a few TikTok videos of elaborately designed dorms being revealed to their gasping undergrads went viral, the internet at large began to obsess over the perfectly curated color schemes, matching monogrammed pillows and, one can assume, hefty price tags for touches like custom built-ins and a shelf to hold their designer bags .

The fascination follows a broader online trend toward a cultural obsession with big public university culture in the South (see: # RushTok ). But the dorm designers I spoke to also believe that the desire for a custom and comfortable room is unique to the current generation of college students. Sure, they want to post beautiful photos to social media to keep up with their peers, but they also value their personal space in a different way.

"Having a beautiful dorm space helps me to feel more at home," Kamryn Hall, a 19-year-old sophomore at Florida State, tells me. When she's not studying, Hall creates content geared toward other college students and has been sharing her journey of designing her second-year dorm room.

"It isn't necessarily about the aesthetics," she says about her choice to invest in her space, which includes a pink ruffled duvet and a custom LED name sign . "It's more about self-expression and getting to showcase everything that I love in a space that's mine and having some feel of individuality, especially when you're in a shared space."

Shannan Bower has worked as an interior designer in Fort Worth, Texas, for 18 years, and added dorm services to her repertoire several years ago. She thinks the fact that Gen Z spent so much time indoors and at home during the pandemic gave them an appreciation of " how your environment can affect the way you feel."

"It's not just about making something pretty for social media," she tells me. "Students want personalization, comfort and a space they can come back to at the end of a long day and genuinely feel at home in. A dorm doesn't have to just be four walls, a bed and a few posters anymore."

Still, for those of us who grew up in that "four walls and a few posters" era, the juxtaposition between what we had and what we see online now can be hilariously stark. Content creator Melanie Ressa, who is 35, jokingly joined the conversation on Instagram by posting a photo of her old dorm, which had one piece of "art": a beer pong poster. She's endlessly fascinated by the rooms she keeps seeing online, she says, because she considers college to be a time when your life should be anything but curated.

"My hot take is that these girls have their entire lives to be adults," she says. "Dorm rooms are not supposed to be perfectly crafted design spaces. What happened to the display of liquor bottle trophies, stolen street signs and posters bought from Spencer's?"

Then there's the debate over costs. After videos of "dorm reveals" from one designer, Shelly Gates of Mississippi, went viral on TikTok last year, she revealed to People that her services can cost up to $20,000 for a custom room. But Fox and Cabale say you don't have to spend a fortune, and most people don't. The extremes may be going viral, but their clients are shopping on Amazon and at HomeGoods (their consultations start at just $100).

Bower advises her clients to invest the most in the items that will be functional for the most important parts of college life: studying and sleeping (what did you think I was going to say?).

"Invest in comfortable bedding and a good mattress topper because sleep is incredibly important for a college student," she says. "Make sure you have functional storage so you're not constantly living in clutter, and create a study space where you can actually spread out and focus."

Fox and Cabale have found that creating a beautiful living space, with the help of parents and/or a decorator, is often a cathartic experience for their young clients. Leaving home and attending college, after all, is a huge life change, and Fox likes to believe that making something cozy and chic can ease jitters for both moms and daughters before they step into the next chapter.

"We feel like it's giving the moms [a chance to] bridge that gap between them being at home and launching them," she says. "It's also giving the girls a lot of confidence and comfort in their new space. … They're really proud of what they're creating."

"My hot take is that these girls have their entire lives to be adults," she says. "Dorm rooms are not supposed to be perfectly crafted design spaces. What happened to the display of liquor bottle trophies, stolen street signs and posters bought from Spencer's?"

Then there's the debate over costs. After videos of "dorm reveals" from one designer, Shelly Gates of Mississippi, went viral on TikTok last year, she revealed to People that her services can cost up to $20,000 for a custom room. But Fox and Cabale say you don't have to spend a fortune, and most people don't. The extremes may be going viral, but their clients are shopping on Amazon and at HomeGoods (their consultations start at just $100).
Bower advises her clients to invest the most in the items that will be functional for the most important parts of college life: studying and sleeping (what did you think I was going to say?).

"Invest in comfortable bedding and a good mattress topper because sleep is incredibly important for a college student," she says. "Make sure you have functional storage so you're not constantly living in clutter, and create a study space where you can actually spread out and focus."

Fox and Cabale have found that creating a beautiful living space, with the help of parents and/or a decorator, is often a cathartic experience for their young clients. Leaving home and attending college, after all, is a huge life change, and Fox likes to believe that making something cozy and chic can ease jitters for both moms and daughters before they step into the next chapter.

"We feel like it's giving the moms [a chance to] bridge that gap between them being at home and launching them," she says. "It's also giving the girls a lot of confidence and comfort in their new space. … They're really proud of what they're creating."

articles.title: China, India hold border talks, agree to continue search for boundary settlement
articles.summary: BEIJING, Aug 25 (Reuters) - China and India agreed on Tuesday to continue dialogue and seek a "fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable settlement" of their...
articles.body:
BEIJING, Aug 25 (Reuters) - China and India agreed on Tuesday to continue dialogue and seek a "fair, reasonable and mutually acceptable settlement" ‌of their border issue after talks between senior diplomats in ‌Beijing.

The world's two most populous nations, both nuclear powers, share a roughly 3,800-km (2,400-mile), largely undemarcated ​and disputed border in the Himalayas.

Chinese Foreign Minister Wang Yi and India's National Security Advisor Ajit Doval had "comprehensive, in-depth, friendly and candid" discussions on border affairs and bilateral ties, China's foreign ministry said in a statement.

Wang said China-India ‌relations were no longer ⁠only of bilateral importance but carried global and strategic significance, saying the two neighbours should strengthen communication and reduce ⁠their differences.

The Indian Embassy in China confirmed in a post on X that the two sides had reviewed bilateral ties and had discussed ways to ​further expand ​cooperation and maintain stability and peace ​in border areas.

Ties between Beijing ‌and New Delhi have gradually improved in recent years following a deadly 2020 border clash, which led to a four-year military standoff before a disengagement agreement was reached in October 2024.

Last year Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi visited China for the first time in seven years, in a sign ‌of a thaw in relations. More recently, ​a fresh border-related dispute triggered sharp diplomatic ​exchanges between the two rivals.

"Both ​sides should learn from historical experience, place the border ‌issue in an appropriate position in ​bilateral relations, and ​move forward without stagnation, regression, or deviation," Wang was quoted as telling Doval at Tuesday's meeting.

The two countries have agreed to hold ​the next round of ‌border talks in India in 2027, the Chinese statement added.

(Reporting by ​Beijing Newsroom, additional reporting by Bipasha Dey in Bengaluru; Editing ​by Alex Richardson and Gareth Jones)

articles.title: Sunderland University relocated gallery set for first exhibition
articles.summary: The Northern Gallery for Contemporary Art opens in September after the closure of the Glass Centre.
articles.body:
The first exhibition of an art gallery forced to move to new premises has been announced.

The Northern Gallery for Contemporary Art (NGCA) is moving to the Culture House in Sunderland on 12 September, opening with an exhibition on local artist Audrey Amiss.

The University of Sunderland, which runs the gallery, said Kitchen Sink Realism would feature previously unseen paintings and drawings, as well as archival material by the late Sunderland-born artist.

The gallery was previously housed at the National Glass Centre, which shut in July after the university said it could not afford building repairs.

Despite being a prolific artist, it was only after her death in 2013 that Amiss' breadth of work came to light.

She is known for her campaigning against harmful treatment in the mental health system, after a crisis she suffered as a student in the 1950s.

Her exhibition will be on display until 17 January, and the university is offering printmaking workshops on the opening weekend.

Kevin Petrie, professor of creative practice at the university, said the gallery was a "long-standing asset" for students.

"It gives them the chance to work alongside the exhibition curator, and in many cases artists themselves, to learn first-hand about careers and professional practice in the arts," he said.

Culture House will also house a library, podcasting studios and a sky garden when it opens.

articles.title: Israeli military sent US universities millions for weapons research: Report
articles.summary: Middle East News: The Israeli Ministry of Defense and Israeli defence companies have channelled millions of dollars into weapons-related research at US universities, mu.
articles.body: The Israeli Ministry of Defense and Israeli defence companies have channelled millions of dollars into weapons-related research at US universities, much of it through funding arrangements that were not consistently disclosed in federal databases, according to an investigation by Drop Site News.The investigation found financial links between Israelâs Ministry of Defense, weapons manufacturers and dozens of American universities over the past two decades. These included research grants, tuition payments and other forms of institutional funding, with records dating from 2004 to 2025.According to Drop Site News, an analysis of university and state audit records identified more than $15 million in funding linked to the Israeli Ministry of Defense or Israeli defence companies that was either unreported or reported inconsistently. The publication said the actual figure could be higher because some university records did not disclose funding amounts, while others contained conflicting information.The investigation identified ties involving prominent institutions including Columbia, Cornell, Princeton, Harvard, Northwestern, Georgia Tech, the University of Connecticut, the University of Maryland and the University of California, Berkeley.Among the Israeli companies involved were defence giants Elbit Systems, Rafael and Israel Aerospace Industries, with records showing sponsorship of research projects related to military technologies.At the University of Connecticut, for example, federal audit records show an Israeli Ministry of Defense-funded project titled âImpact Point Prediction Research for Short & Medium Range Thrusting Projectilesâ. The project received $668,456 across nine fiscal years between 2013 and 2023. Another project, âHigh Sensitivity SQUIDs for Magnetic Field Detectionâ, received $251,336 over the same period.US law requires universities receiving federal assistance to report foreign gifts and contracts worth at least $250,000 in a calendar year. However, Drop Site found that some Israeli funding did not consistently appear in the federal disclosure system.The findings come amid renewed tensions between Israel and the US over Israeli military actions in the region. Axios recently reported that Israeli strikes on Syriaâs Abu al-Duhur airbase frustrated senior Trump administration officials, with Washington calling the operation an âunnecessary escalationâ.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Gun-running ship located 78 years after being sunk by Israeli military
articles.summary: In June 1948, Israeli forces opened fire and sank the boat in waters off Tel Aviv on the orders of David Ben Gurion, Israel's first prime minister.
articles.body:
Israel announced on Monday it had recovered the wreckage of the Altalena, an arms-smuggling boat whose sinking by the Israeli military just after the state's founding in 1948 exposed divisions that persist today.

The Altalena had set sail from France loaded with weapons packed for the Irgun, the militant Zionist force that conducted attacks against the British colonial authorities and the local Palestinian population in the quest to establish Israel.

In June 1948, Israeli forces opened fire and sank the boat in waters off Tel Aviv on the orders of David Ben Gurion, Israel's first prime minister. He wanted to exert his authority and prevent the emergence of any paramilitary rival to the Israeli military in the month-old state, which was in the throes of war with neighboring Arab countries.

"At 12:30 am, at a depth of 503 meters, west of the coast of Israel, the Altalena ship was located intact — 78 years after that painful and seminal event that shook the young State of Israel," Heritage Minister Amihai Eliyahu said.

Sixteen Irgun members and three Israeli soldiers were killed. Irgun chief Menachem Begin asked his fighters to surrender to Israeli authorities with words that would become famous: "There will be no civil war with the enemy at our gates."

After the violence, the burned-out vessel remained off the Tel Aviv coast before eventually being towed out to sea and sunk, according to the Jerusalem Post , which published a computer image of the remains of the ship on the seafloor.

The conflict pitted against each other the two political blocs that would define Israel. Begin became prime minister in 1977, ushering in the rise of right-wing nationalists and sweeping out the socialist movement launched under Ben Gurion.

Eliyahu, who announced the salvaging of the Altalena, hails from the far-right, which has taken power as part of a government led by Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.

He called the Altalena "the story of a deep national wound, and the story of the historical responsibility that Menachem Begin showed when he prevented a civil war."

"A country that is not afraid to touch on the painful chapters of its history is a stronger country," he said.

Israel erected a monument to the fallen Altalena militants in 2008 on the Tel Aviv seafront and has been searching for the wreckage for years, with crews often working in secrecy.

It was not immediately known what would happen to the ship's wreckage.

"Finding Altalena is not an opportunity to renew old disputes," the Ben Gurion Heritage Institute wrote on social media after the ship's discovery. "It is an opportunity to remind why statism is not a slogan — but a condition for the existence of a state."

articles.title: Syria's Kurdish-led SDF dissolves as part of integration with Damascus
articles.summary: DAMASCUS, Aug 25 (Reuters) - The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces has been dissolved, the armed militant group's leader said on Tuesday, a major step in...
articles.body:
SDF commander Mazloum Abdi delivers a speech during a celebration marking the centenary of the city of Qamishli

DAMASCUS, Aug 25 (Reuters) - The Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces has been dissolved, the armed militant group's leader said ‌on Tuesday, a major step in the integration plan ‌agreed on earlier this year with the Islamist-led government in Damascus.

"We announce ​today the end of the mission of the Syrian Democratic Forces and announce with full responsibility its dissolution as an independent military force," SDF commander Mazloum Abdi said in a televised speech.

The ‌government and the ⁠group, which helped defeat the Islamic State with U.S. backing and held parts of northern and ⁠eastern Syria, agreed in January to a phased integration of Kurdish fighters into the state, a plan Washington called a "historic milestone".

The ​deal came ​shortly after government forces under ​President Ahmed al-Sharaa launched a ‌lightning offensive in January, taking swathes of the areas the SDF held.

Abdi said that the announcement followed an agreement with Sharaa after the integration of the group's forces into the army.

The Kurdish People's Protection Units, which formed the core of ‌the SDF, had already been integrated ​within state forces with its commander, ​Sipan Hamo, appointed in ​March deputy defence minister for the country's eastern ‌territories.

The SDF dissolution comes as the ​new leaders ​in Damascus seek to resolve internal strife and rebuild Syria, with support from Washington, after nearly 14 years of ​civil war and ‌decades of isolation under former President Bashar al-Assad's rule.

(Reporting ​by Orhan Qereman and Nayera Abdallah, Writing by Nayera ​Abdallah; Editing by Alistair Bell)

articles.title: UN chief condemns Haiti gang attack that killed at least 47
articles.summary: UN Secretary General António Guterres has condemned a gang attack in Haiti that killed at least 47 people, including 22 who were reportedly executed at a chu...
articles.body:
UN Secretary General António Guterres has condemned a gang attack in Haiti that killed at least 47 people, including 22 who were reportedly executed at a church compound where they had sought shelter.

The attack took place at the weekend in Kenscoff, a community on the outskirts of the capital Port-au-Prince.

"The relentless gang attacks on communities and the loss of lives underscore the alarming security conditions in Haiti and reinforce the urgent need to intensify Haitian and international security efforts to counter gangs," Guterres' spokesman, Stéphane Dujarric, said in a statement on Tuesday.

Guterres also reiterated his call for Haitian authorities to "ensure that those responsible for such attacks are held accountable," including through specialized judicial units recently established with international support to investigate mass crimes.

According to the UN Integrated Office in Haiti (BINUH), more than 50 people were also abducted and 22 injured in Sunday night's attack on Kenscoff, around 10 kilometres south of Port-au-Prince.

The attackers targeted the centre of the community, setting numerous homes on fire and storming a church compound where displaced people had sought shelter, broadcaster Radio Télé Galaxie reported.

The UN's Dujarric said it was believed that 22 of the victims were killed at the church complex.

Police eventually managed to push back the attackers and regain control of the area.

Haiti's transitional government confirmed the attack but did not provide a death toll. It described the violence as a "heinous criminal attack," placed security forces on the highest level of alert and deployed reinforcements.

articles.title: A British Army commander testing war robots says they aren't always the right tool for the job
articles.summary: Uncrewed ground vehicles, or UGVs, can present logistics, power, navigation, and control challenges for soldiers, he said.
articles.body:
A British Army commander says ground robots can be useful but come with drawbacks.

UGVs can create logistics, power, navigation, and control challenges for troops.

Ukraine shows their value may be mainly in dangerous, specialized missions that protect soldiers.

The commander of a British Army battalion tasked with experimenting with new technologies said that his unit has tested out dozens of ground robots. He concluded that they can be useful, but only for certain missions. And they come with a long list of challenges.

As Western militaries rush to absorb lessons from the war in Ukraine and integrate more uncrewed systems into their respective forces, soldiers are finding that some systems might look good on paper but aren't effective in all combat scenarios.

Ground robots , in particular, can face weight, navigation, cost, and power constraints that raise questions about when and how they should be used. In Ukraine's case, the systems have seen use in logistics operations, replacing soldiers in highly dangerous areas of the battlefield, but soldiers have also said they're not a catch-all solution.

At a recent US Army-led exercise at Fort Irwin in California, a handful of American allies and partners gathered with US forces to experiment with new systems in a simulated conflict against a near-peer adversary. The British Army's experimentation unit, the 2nd Battalion, The Yorkshire Regiment, was present for the event alongside the unit that will take over their experimentation role, the 1st Battalion Irish Guards.

During the recent exercise, Lt. Col. John Black, commander of the 2nd Battalion of the Yorkshire Regiment, told Business Insider that he and his unit have seen and tested a wide range of uncrewed ground vehicles, or UGVs.

"Any use case you can think of, we've tried it," he said, adding that they're not just driving it around to see how it works; rather, they are focused on "trying to employ it in a tactical scenario."

Through that experimentation, Black and his troops have encountered problems that can make UGVs difficult to use. For instance, many of the medium- to large-sized UGVs they tested required trailers or flatbed trucks to transport. Depending on how soldiers are moving and what they're carrying, that creates a logistical burden.

And once they've moved it into position, troops still have to figure out how to get it into the fight.

"Even if they've got quite long range and good speed, there's still going to be a process where you're moving them into the fight," Black said.

UGVs can also create power and refueling challenges. Depending on the system, specifically it's size, range, and capabilities, troops in the field may need to carry extra batteries, generators, or fuel — or periodically bring the robot back to a charging point.

Remote control introduces another set of problems, from maintaining a reliable connection to keeping the robot on course. The systems can also struggle with difficult terrain .

Often, their advertised range doesn't translate cleanly to real-world conditions, such as uneven ground. Obstacles "confound" most UGVs, Black said.

Whether UGVs can rely on autonomous features is a particularly thorny subject. Autonomy has become a major area of interest across uncrewed capabilities, but Black said some manufacturers have moved away from offering autonomous UGVs.

"We have seen, over the last few years, these vendors stop offering autonomous ones because it's unworkable," he said, explaining that such autonomous features can result in the system being more expensive and difficult to use.

Despite those limitations, Black said there are certain situations where he sees value, including breaches and mine removal .

Both missions are incredibly dangerous for soldiers. For that reason, militaries have been using remote-controlled technologies for breaching fortified positions and removing mines for decades. Certain UGVs coming online now could be the next evolution in that technology, but other methods could prove more practical.

Ground robots are seeing growing use in Ukraine, sometimes operating as a safer option than sending soldiers into "the kill zone" to deliver supplies and ammo. Ukraine has also used them offensively, such as driving one equipped with a gun off a drone boat in a first-of-its-kind robotic amphibious assault.

However, their growing use in that fight hasn't settled the debate on their overall usefulness. Black indicated that they might be a niche tool, most effective only in those cases where keeping a soldier out of harm's way matters most.

If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo.

Remote control introduces another set of problems, from maintaining a reliable connection to keeping the robot on course. The systems can also struggle with difficult terrain .
Often, their advertised range doesn't translate cleanly to real-world conditions, such as uneven ground. Obstacles "confound" most UGVs, Black said.

Whether UGVs can rely on autonomous features is a particularly thorny subject. Autonomy has become a major area of interest across uncrewed capabilities, but Black said some manufacturers have moved away from offering autonomous UGVs.

"We have seen, over the last few years, these vendors stop offering autonomous ones because it's unworkable," he said, explaining that such autonomous features can result in the system being more expensive and difficult to use.
Despite those limitations, Black said there are certain situations where he sees value, including breaches and mine removal .

Both missions are incredibly dangerous for soldiers. For that reason, militaries have been using remote-controlled technologies for breaching fortified positions and removing mines for decades. Certain UGVs coming online now could be the next evolution in that technology, but other methods could prove more practical.

Ground robots are seeing growing use in Ukraine, sometimes operating as a safer option than sending soldiers into "the kill zone" to deliver supplies and ammo. Ukraine has also used them offensively, such as driving one equipped with a gun off a drone boat in a first-of-its-kind robotic amphibious assault.

However, their growing use in that fight hasn't settled the debate on their overall usefulness. Black indicated that they might be a niche tool, most effective only in those cases where keeping a soldier out of harm's way matters most.
If you enjoyed this story, be sure to follow Business Insider on Yahoo.

articles.title: Who has been the Bengals Preseason MVP?
articles.summary: It’s been a fun preseason for the Bengals, and guys like Colbie Young are a big reason why.
articles.body:
The preseason is nearly complete for the Cincinnati Bengals , who will face the Philadelphia Eagles on Friday night. After that, all 32 NFL teams will begin trimming down their rosters to 53 men before the deadline on August 30 at 6 PM ET.

For the Bengals, it's been a fun preseason thus far as they've rolled toward a 2-0 start, thanks in large part to several players who could be considered the team's MVP of the preseason.

So, we want you to tell us who has been the Bengals preseason MVP thus far.

Former CFL wide receiver Dohnte Meyers has been the surprise of camp and the preseason, going from facing an uphill climb just to make the practice squad to now likely securing a spot on the 53-man roster.

Fourth-round rookie Colbie Young has also been an impact pass-catcher and could be setting himself up to play meaningful snaps in Year 1.

On defense, seventh-round rookie Landon Robinson has been a pass-rushing force on the interior as he too looks to secure one of those final roster spots.

Edge rusher Isaiah Foskey has quietly racked up eight total pressures and a 77.0 PFF grade this preseason as he fights for one of the final edge spots.

Veteran linebacker and Super Bowl champion Swayze Bozeman has made some noise at linebacker and could sneak onto the 53-man roster when it's all said and done.

So, who would you crown the 2026 Bengals Preseason MVP thus far? Let us know your pick below!

Welcome to SB Nation Reacts, a survey of fans across the NFL. Throughout the year, we ask questions of the most plugged-in Bengals fans and fans across the country. And as always, WHO DEY!

articles.title: Back to school: How to save on uniform costs
articles.summary: From baby banks to supermarket deals, there are many ways parents can ease the back-to-school burden.
articles.body:
Back to school can stir up many emotions for parents, including anxiety about the extra costs it brings.

Almost half of parents said they're worried about the cost of school uniforms, according to research by the charity Save the Children and the Baby Bank Alliance network.

And a third of the 2,000 parents polled said they've sacrificed things for themselves to meet back-to-school costs like uniforms, bags or books.

New rules limiting the number of items branded with a school logo to three per child come into force in September, aimed at helping ease the financial burden.

From baby banks to council grants, here are ways parents can ease the cost of kitting out their kids for school.

Save the Children said the new uniform rules are a "good start" but back-to-school costs remain a concern for families across almost all income brackets.

The government said schools should make second-hand uniforms accessible to parents.

"Speak to a teacher you trust, and explain that the costs are difficult," said Megan Meek-O'Connor, head of England and Westminster at Save the Children.

Many schools have uniform hubs, swap shops and sales just before term starts, and hardship funds.

In London, the School Uniform Reuse Network launched earlier this year, giving schools practical advice to start or improve their own swap shops.

During its first term of operation, it saw more than 1,500 items reused across 24 schools.

Parents of older children may not realise a so-called baby bank can help them, but many of the 400 support hubs across the UK provide uniforms for children up to and through secondary school.

In its latest survey of members, the Baby Bank Alliance found school uniform was reported as a priority item for the first time.

Late summer is one of the busiest times for Little Stars Shrewsbury - just over half the children helped since June have been given uniform support.

Hannah Stoddart, operations manager at Little Stars Shrewsbury, said families come to them in varying circumstances. A child starting school might need fully kitting out, while an older pupil may just need to replace one or two items.

Stoddart stressed that while the summer holidays "take their toll", the charity provides help all year.

"So when they've had that growth spurt, when they've scuffed their shoes or they've ripped their trousers or they need a winter coat, that's something they can come back to us for as well," she said.

The relaxed rules on uniform branding mean parents can purchase more items from supermarkets and charity shops, said Save the Children's Meek-O'Connor.

Pre-loved items are usually what "kids have grown out of quickly rather than things that are poor quality", she said.

Parents can cheaply stock up on frequent-wear items with supermarket bundle deals, while the charity Family Action suggested they team up to bulk buy items that would otherwise take them over budget.

According to research from the bank Nationwide, a third of parents said they buy uniform from supermarkets, a third shop around for the best value and 23% purchase larger sizes so items last longer.

Kate Steere, parent and consumer editor at the comparison site Finder, said sports kit costs can be "brutal".

"I always encourage parents to tap into their club's community. Families with older kids are usually eager to pass down gear," she said.

"My boys' football team runs a summer sale for second-hand kit, and apps like Vinted or Facebook Marketplace are goldmines."

You may be able to get a grant from your local authority if your income is below a certain threshold or you're receiving certain benefits.

These can be worth up to Â£200 per child.

Eligibility and how much you can get can vary according to where in the UK you live, so it is best to check with your council directly.

Struggling with uniform costs is common and people shouldn't feel ashamed if they need to ask for help, said Meek-O'Connor.

"Uniform is supposed to be about making school kind of more accessible, more equal... it should be something positive," she said.

articles.title: Game Thread: Rangers (66-66) at White Sox (68-63)
articles.summary: Anthony Kay and the South Siders look to rebound from Monday’s rough loss
articles.body:
A blowout loss is a tough way to start a series at home in a playoff race, but the South Siders hope to flush Monday's game and come out strong behind Anthony Kay today. After defeating the Sox yesterday, the Rangers now hold a half-game lead over the Houston Astros in the AL West, while Chicago 's lead in the AL Central has shrunk to just 2 1/2 games over the Cleveland Guardians . The Guardians have rebounded from their rough stretch, winning seven of their last 10 and riding a five-game winning streak after defeating the Los Angeles Angels yesterday. The Angels, of course, had opportunities to come back but naturally didn't.

The South Siders are 5-5 in their last 10, and the offense has been struggling as a whole lately, basically living and dying by the long ball as we've seen in the last several games. In August, the White Sox are hitting just .208 with runners in scoring position as a team — the second-worst average in baseball over that stretch — while also racking up the most strikeouts (70). It also probably doesn't help that both Colson Montgomery and Munetaka Murakami are building Strikeout City from the ground up, with Colson leading MLB in Ks over the last two weeks (24 in 51 ABs) and Mune's 21 ranking third in baseball. Woof.

With both the rotation and bullpen continuing to struggle, the pitching staff took another hit when the White Sox announced that Huascar Brazobán is headed to the IL with a left lat strain. Righthander Jonathan Cannon is being called up from Triple-A Charlotte to help fill the hole. Jonathan Cannon is most certainly not the answer, but at this point, the front office seems ready to try anything.

Prior to tonight’s game vs. Texas, the Chicago White Sox placed right-handed pitcher Huáscar Brazobán on the 15-day injured list with a left lat strain and recalled right-handed pitcher Jonathan Cannon from Class AAA Charlotte. — Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) August 25, 2026

Prior to tonight’s game vs. Texas, the Chicago White Sox placed right-handed pitcher Huáscar Brazobán on the 15-day injured list with a left lat strain and recalled right-handed pitcher Jonathan Cannon from Class AAA Charlotte.

The only other roster update for today is that our sweet (mostly) clutch Andrew Benintendi has been placed on the bereavement list, and Rikuu Nishida will rejoin the team in his absence. We send our thoughts to Andrew and his family during this time.

Prior to tonight’s game vs. Texas, the Chicago White Sox placed outfielder Andrew Benintendi on the Bereavement/Family Medical Emergency List and recalled infielder/outfielder Rikuu Nishida from Class AAA Charlotte. — Chicago White Sox (@whitesox) August 25, 2026

Prior to tonight’s game vs. Texas, the Chicago White Sox placed outfielder Andrew Benintendi on the Bereavement/Family Medical Emergency List and recalled infielder/outfielder Rikuu Nishida from Class AAA Charlotte.

Regardless of what the masses may think, lefthander Anthony Kay has been solid for the Good Guys and is probably the second-best starter they currently have behind Sean Burke . Kay will make his 25th start of the season and has a 3.96 ERA and a 1.327 WHIP over 127 1/3 innings. He seems to keep improving, and in August alone, Kay has allowed just seven earned runs over 23 2/3 innings (four starts), good for a cool 2.66 ERA and a 2-1 record. If you ask me, his great outing against the Atlanta Braves last week went unrewarded because the offense was nowhere to be found.

Hopefully, the bats — or really anybody not named Miguel Vargas or Tristan Peters — can wake up to provide some early run support for Kay, but they will have a tough matchup with righthander Jacob deGrom on the mound. Peters has homered in three straight games, however, so let's see if he can make it four.

With Benintendi unavailable and a righty on the mound, Sam Antonacci is taking over as the DH and leading off today. Peters will shift to left field in Benintendi's place, while Brenton Doyle slots into center field and bats eighth. With those changes, today's lineup is almost identical to Monday's, and as we know, Will Venable loves the righty-lefty matchups. Still, I would be remiss not to mention Randal Grichuk 's career performance against deGrom: In 14 plate appearances, Grichuk has dominated. He's slashed .385/.429/1.000 with two home runs, amassing a 1.429 OPS.

deGrom is also making his 25th start of the season and holds a 3.77 ERA across 126 2/3 innings. The 38-year-old still has zero problems striking guys out and has rung up 157 batters this season. His 30.3% strikeout rate ranks in the top 8% of MLB pitchers. deGrom's fastball averages around 97 mph, though his off-speed pitches — slider, curveball and changeup — all fool batters, with all three pitches generating a whiff rate above 40%. His slider seems to be his most effective pitch, with opponents batting just .163 and slugging a measly .227 against it.

After being ejected from yesterday's game for heckling the ump, Joc Pederson will get another day off, with Justin Foscue remaining in the leadoff spot after a decent performance Monday. Corey Seager has been swinging a hot bat lately, and after two doubles and three RBIs yesterday, that is now apparent. In the past two weeks, Seager has the third-highest batting average in MLB (.419) and the sixth-highest OPS (1.164), and he's actually hit lefties better this year (.256 BA vs. .222 against righties).

First pitch is scheduled for 6:40 p.m. CDT, and it should be a beautiful night for a ballgame: 78º with partly cloudy skies. Watch on CHSN or listen on ESPN Chicago 1000 AM.

articles.title: Stevenage 0-3 Reading: Samba Rhythm Starts To Play
articles.summary: Jacob Brown, Paddy Lane and Randell Williams were on the scoresheet as Reading advanced to the third round of the League Cup.
articles.body:
"As the samba rhythm starts to play, dance with me, make me sway…"

So goes Paddy Lane 's chant. It's been sung out of optimism more than expectation in the year or so since he joined – the former Portsmouth winger struggling to show us what he's capable of on a consistent basis.

But tonight, at long last, this was absolutely Lane's night. It wasn't just about a single dramatic moment though, like when he netted winners last season over Port Vale or Bradford City. Rather, this was the kind of game that made you think that a big talent – one with so much potential to offer – may now have truly found his feet.

Would the Lane of last season have sent in that accurate low cross for Jacob Brown to convert for 1-0? Would he have cheekily lobbed Filip Marschall for 2-0? Football often comes down simply to being about confidence, and Lane demonstrated plenty of that throughout this evening's game.

But this was a pleasingly confident display all round from the Royals, who are now properly up and running for the season, and have a spot in the third round of the League Cup to look forward to. Although penalty shootout success is a victory of sorts, and we'd managed two of those already this season, tonight was Reading's first proper win.

And what better way to get it than in this kind of style? Three good goals from open play scored, none conceded (for the second match in a row) and a convincing attacking display that bore all the hallmarks of what Leam Richardson was trying to build over the summer: quick, direct and quality wide play.

The goals themselves were great examples of that. The first: a low cross from a winger (Lane setting up Brown). The second: a goal put away by a winger (Lane). The third: a winger putting the ball on a plate for another winger at the back post (Kyreece Lisbie, albeit playing up front in a 3-5-2, passing for Williams).

Not just a good performance then, but everything (as far as I can tell) going to plan. That samba rhythm wasn't confined just to Lane after all.

Richardson made nine changes from Saturday's 0-0 draw at AFC Wimbledon, with Joel Pereira and Benn Ward the only survivors. Conor Masterson and George Earthy were given full debuts, while there were also a number of first-team players included on a strong-looking bench.

Reading (4-2-3-1): Pereira; Ahmed, Masterson, Ward, Dorsett ; Fraser, Savage; Williams, Earthy, Lane; Brown Subs: Stevens, Roberts, Wing, Rinomhota, Stokes, Osho, Kyerewaa, Lisbie

Reading (4-2-3-1): Pereira; Ahmed, Masterson, Ward, Dorsett ; Fraser, Savage; Williams, Earthy, Lane; Brown

Subs: Stevens, Roberts, Wing, Rinomhota, Stokes, Osho, Kyerewaa, Lisbie

After a slightly shaky start in the early moments of the game, when debutant Masterson had to be on his toes, Reading took a 0-1 lead in the ninth minute. Liam Fraser pinged the ball out wide to Lane on the the left, whose low cross to the near post was diverted in by Brown.

The Royals played with confident at this point and looked to push for a second. The pairing down the right of full-back Ashqar Ahmed and winger Williams was a particularly potent-looking one, just as it had been in pre-season at Crawley Town.

A quarter of an hour or so after the opener, Reading doubled their lead. This time a long ball down the left wasn't dealt with properly by a Stevenage defender, whose loose header dropped for Lane. He still had a fair amount to do to beat the onrushing 'keeper, but dinked the ball over Marschall and home for 0-2 .

There was no other major action in the remainder of a positive half. The Royals generally looked bright in possession and did well enough to restrict a fairly limited attacking effort from the hosts, with Pereira not called into any heroics.

The second 45 was, on the whole, a much more even affair than the first, with the hosts coming fairly close to finding a way back into the game a few times.

That started off pretty early as Stevenage managed to put the Royals' defence under extended pressure soon after the restart. They even had the ball in the net not long after the interval, tucking it home from a deep free-kick on their left – but thankfully from an offside position.

Around 10 minutes later, more opportunities came Stevenage's way. Pereira did well to parry a powerful shot from the edge of the area on one occasion, and soon after watched a header (set up by a cross from our right) go wide of the post.

Down the other end though, Reading were carrying a threat going forwards of their own. This was a crucial difference from previous games this season, in which the Royals had looked good in the first half but struggled to maintain offensive consistency in the second.

The first example of that was a smart run in behind from Earthy a few minutes after the restart, getting on the edge of a Brown flicked header before forcing a save at the near post. The summer signing had other opportunities midway through the half – both of them being shots blocked inside the Stevenage area.

Reading seemed to be fading somewhat in the last 20 minutes, with the hosts in the ascendancy. The Royals' inability to kill the game off earlier in the half perhaps emboldened the home side, who piled more and more pressure on the visitors.

Richardson made his first change in the 81st minute, swapping Earthy off for Lisbie. That also meant a switch to a 3-5-2: Lane slotting in as a left-wing-back as the back four shunted over, with Williams going into midfield and Lisbie partnering Brown up front.

Ward then almost inadvertently helped Stevenage to halve the deficit. A low cross from Stevenage's left ricocheted off the defender inside the six-yard area, towards goal, but fortunately Pereira was able to block the ball.

Nervy times indeed, but Reading soon killed the game. Brown picked the ball up in space, slipped Lisbie in behind with a cute pass, and his low cross to the back post set up one of the easiest finishes Williams will have in his career. 0-3 , job done.

With the match killed off, Richardson made one more change. Lane was given a well deserved standing ovation from a jubilant away end as he was replaced by Daniel Kyerewaa – whose spot in the first team he could well soon take.

So, at the fifth time of asking, Reading finally have a normal-time win in 2026/27. What's more, we've got a mini cup run on our hands, and hopefully we'll have an exciting draw in the next round to look forward to.

Besides the obvious morale boost of a good performance and comfortable scoreline, Richardson will also be pleased with a few aspects of the Royals' performance: ruthlessness with chances, more consistent attacking threat across the 90 minutes, quality from out wide, not collapsing after the break, riding out the pressure Stevenage offered, and squad players staking a convincing claim to regular minutes in the league.

All in all then, surely exactly the kind of performance Richardson has been trying to establish in the last few months. The tricky next step: getting Reading to do this regularly in the league.

Although penalty shootout success is a victory of sorts, and we'd managed two of those already this season, tonight was Reading's first proper win.

And what better way to get it than in this kind of style? Three good goals from open play scored, none conceded (for the second match in a row) and a convincing attacking display that bore all the hallmarks of what Leam Richardson was trying to build over the summer: quick, direct and quality wide play.

The goals themselves were great examples of that. The first: a low cross from a winger (Lane setting up Brown). The second: a goal put away by a winger (Lane). The third: a winger putting the ball on a plate for another winger at the back post (Kyreece Lisbie, albeit playing up front in a 3-5-2, passing for Williams).
Not just a good performance then, but everything (as far as I can tell) going to plan. That samba rhythm wasn't confined just to Lane after all.

Richardson made nine changes from Saturday's 0-0 draw at AFC Wimbledon, with Joel Pereira and Benn Ward the only survivors. Conor Masterson and George Earthy were given full debuts, while there were also a number of first-team players included on a strong-looking bench.
Reading (4-2-3-1): Pereira; Ahmed, Masterson, Ward, Dorsett ; Fraser, Savage; Williams, Earthy, Lane; Brown Subs: Stevens, Roberts, Wing, Rinomhota, Stokes, Osho, Kyerewaa, Lisbie
Reading (4-2-3-1): Pereira; Ahmed, Masterson, Ward, Dorsett ; Fraser, Savage; Williams, Earthy, Lane; Brown
Subs: Stevens, Roberts, Wing, Rinomhota, Stokes, Osho, Kyerewaa, Lisbie

After a slightly shaky start in the early moments of the game, when debutant Masterson had to be on his toes, Reading took a 0-1 lead in the ninth minute. Liam Fraser pinged the ball out wide to Lane on the the left, whose low cross to the near post was diverted in by Brown.

The Royals played with confident at this point and looked to push for a second. The pairing down the right of full-back Ashqar Ahmed and winger Williams was a particularly potent-looking one, just as it had been in pre-season at Crawley Town.

A quarter of an hour or so after the opener, Reading doubled their lead. This time a long ball down the left wasn't dealt with properly by a Stevenage defender, whose loose header dropped for Lane. He still had a fair amount to do to beat the onrushing 'keeper, but dinked the ball over Marschall and home for 0-2 .

There was no other major action in the remainder of a positive half. The Royals generally looked bright in possession and did well enough to restrict a fairly limited attacking effort from the hosts, with Pereira not called into any heroics.
The second 45 was, on the whole, a much more even affair than the first, with the hosts coming fairly close to finding a way back into the game a few times.

That started off pretty early as Stevenage managed to put the Royals' defence under extended pressure soon after the restart. They even had the ball in the net not long after the interval, tucking it home from a deep free-kick on their left – but thankfully from an offside position.

Around 10 minutes later, more opportunities came Stevenage's way. Pereira did well to parry a powerful shot from the edge of the area on one occasion, and soon after watched a header (set up by a cross from our right) go wide of the post.

Down the other end though, Reading were carrying a threat going forwards of their own. This was a crucial difference from previous games this season, in which the Royals had looked good in the first half but struggled to maintain offensive consistency in the second.

The first example of that was a smart run in behind from Earthy a few minutes after the restart, getting on the edge of a Brown flicked header before forcing a save at the near post. The summer signing had other opportunities midway through the half – both of them being shots blocked inside the Stevenage area.

Reading seemed to be fading somewhat in the last 20 minutes, with the hosts in the ascendancy. The Royals' inability to kill the game off earlier in the half perhaps emboldened the home side, who piled more and more pressure on the visitors.

Richardson made his first change in the 81st minute, swapping Earthy off for Lisbie. That also meant a switch to a 3-5-2: Lane slotting in as a left-wing-back as the back four shunted over, with Williams going into midfield and Lisbie partnering Brown up front.

Ward then almost inadvertently helped Stevenage to halve the deficit. A low cross from Stevenage's left ricocheted off the defender inside the six-yard area, towards goal, but fortunately Pereira was able to block the ball.

Nervy times indeed, but Reading soon killed the game. Brown picked the ball up in space, slipped Lisbie in behind with a cute pass, and his low cross to the back post set up one of the easiest finishes Williams will have in his career. 0-3 , job done.

With the match killed off, Richardson made one more change. Lane was given a well deserved standing ovation from a jubilant away end as he was replaced by Daniel Kyerewaa – whose spot in the first team he could well soon take.

So, at the fifth time of asking, Reading finally have a normal-time win in 2026/27. What's more, we've got a mini cup run on our hands, and hopefully we'll have an exciting draw in the next round to look forward to.

Besides the obvious morale boost of a good performance and comfortable scoreline, Richardson will also be pleased with a few aspects of the Royals' performance: ruthlessness with chances, more consistent attacking threat across the 90 minutes, quality from out wide, not collapsing after the break, riding out the pressure Stevenage offered, and squad players staking a convincing claim to regular minutes in the league.
All in all then, surely exactly the kind of performance Richardson has been trying to establish in the last few months. The tricky next step: getting Reading to do this regularly in the league.

articles.title: Memphis football vs Mississippi State 2028 game canceled, 2029 game moved to 2034
articles.summary: Memphis football's scheduled home game against Mississippi State in 2028 has been canceled, and a planned 2029 game has been moved to 2034.
articles.body:
Memphis football's scheduled 2028 game against Mississippi State has been canceled and a planned 2029 game in Starkville has been moved to 2034, according to a Mississippi State athletic department spokesperson.

The teams signed a home-and-home deal in 2020 for games in 2028 and 2029. According to the game contract, the team canceling the game (if it's not a mutual agreement) will have to pay $1 million per game to the other team. There is also a clause that would allow a team to cancel the game if its conference causes it to play more games than it did when the game was agreed to. It wasn't immediately clear why the games had been canceled and moved.

The SEC moved from eight to nine conference games starting in the 2026 season.

Memphis did not respond to a request for comment.

The Tigers still have 2028 nonconference games scheduled against Arkansas (road), Toledo (road) and Arkansas State (home).

Scheduling games against power conference opposition has become more and more of a struggle for Memphis , especially after the SEC's move to nine conference games. A planned game against Arkansas that had been scheduled for 2026 was moved to 2030.

Take a look at the Memphis Tigers Fan Fest ahead of 2026-2027 season

The road games at Arkansas in 2028 and 2030 are now the only power conference matchups on Memphis' current future schedules.

The Tigers kick off the 2026 season on the road at UNLV on Aug. 29 (9 p.m. CT, FOX).

Memphis football future nonconference schedules

2026: Arkansas State, at Boise State , at UNLV, UT Martin

2027: at Arkansas State, Southern Miss, at Middle Tennessee State, Toledo

2028: at Arkansas, Arkansas State, at Toledo (one open slot)

2029: at Arkansas State, UNLV (two open slots)

2030: Boise State , at Southern Miss, at Arkansas (one open slot)

2031: at Boise State , (three open slots)

2034: at Mississippi State (three open slots)

Reach sports writer Jonah Dylan at jonah.dylan@commercialappeal.com or on X @thejonahdylan.

articles.title: Pair of Washington First-Years Make Preseason All-Freshmen List
articles.summary: Offensive tackle Kodi Greene and cornerback Jeron Jones will have a healthy amount of expectations placed on their shoulders this upcoming season.
articles.body:
The Washington Huskies football team will have a significant amount of youth front-and-center this season, following a trend that has continued for the program in head coach Jedd Fisch's tenure.

Fisch and the rest of his coaching staff have echoed the sentiment that the "best players will play," regardless of upperclassmen or underclassmen status or experience.

This approach played out positively for Washington last year, which saw two players featured on several end-of-season True Freshmen All-American lists, including offensive guard John Mills and slot receiver Dezmen Roebuck .

The Huskies have two first-year players this season featured on another preseason All-Freshmen list.

A recent article from Clark Brooks of On3 Sports placed offensive tackle Kodi Greene and cornerback Jeron Jones on the publication's preseason list.

Greene's placement on the list comes as little of a shock. He was the top player in Washington's all-time program-best 2026 recruiting class. He was a five-star recruit and was ranked as the 26th-best overall player, third best offensive tackle in the class and third-best player in California, per the 247Sports composite . Greene's ran with the starters at left tackle since practices begun in the spring.

The 18-year-old will be tasked with protecting third-year quarterback Demond Williams Jr.'s blindside. If the signal-caller takes a step forward, as he's looked prepared to do this training camp, the national attention paid toward Greene could end up in him being a near-universal placement on end-of-season All-Freshmen lists, as Mills was last season.

True freshman/1st year Washington offensive lineman and projected starting left tackle Kodi Greene (76) running drills at practice. #Huskies #PurpleReign pic.twitter.com/6RG89QNDb1 — Teren Kowatsch (@Teren_Kowatsch) August 7, 2026

True freshman/1st year Washington offensive lineman and projected starting left tackle Kodi Greene (76) running drills at practice. #Huskies #PurpleReign pic.twitter.com/6RG89QNDb1

Jones was a less-heralded recruit compared to Greene. The Mission Viejo (Calif.) High School graduate was ranked as the 438th-best player in the nation, the 46th-best cornerback in the class and 40th-best player in California, per the 247Sports composite .

Jones has had to work upwards compared to Greene, who received his opportunities with the starters right away. With projected starting nickelback Rahshawn Clark out for the entirety of spring practice, Jones stepped in to take over a decent amount of the reps in the "star" position in defensive coordinator Ryan Walters' defense.

This training camp, Jones has been running with starters as an outside cornerback due to a minor injury to second-year cornerback Dylan Robinson.

When healthy, Washington will likely maintain the status quo of Robinson and fourth-year corner Emmanuel Karnley starting on the outside, with Clark lining back up in the nickel.

However, Jones' performance this spring has likely put him firmly in the rotation for reps this season and he could be the first extra defensive back off the bench in dime package situations for the Huskies.
